definition_zh: 观察；注意到；作科学观测；评论说；遵守；庆祝（节日或仪式）
definition_en: to watch something carefully, to notice, to make a scientific observation, to remark, or to keep a rule or mark a day
core_image: 山顶观测台上，一个人屏住呼吸把望远镜对准同一颗星，每隔一刻钟记下一次位置
scene: 山顶的观测台上，一个人每隔一刻钟记录一次那颗星的位置，直到云层压过来。 Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项：为获取信息而长时间仔细观看；句意为天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。图中可辨识物件：望远镜、记录表、计时器、星图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 观察；注意到；观测；评论；遵守；庆祝

senses.title: To watch with full attention
senses.definition: to watch someone or something closely over time in order to learn how it behaves
senses.definitionCN: 为弄清某人或某物的行为而长时间仔细观看
senses.example: Astronomers observe the same star for months to fix its distance.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家连续数月观测同一颗星，以确定它的距离。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to watch over and heed, so sustained attention rather than a glance is the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为看守并留心，因此持续注意而非一眼扫过，是最古老的一层。

senses.title: To notice
senses.definition: to see or become aware of something, often without looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 看见或意识到某物，往往并非刻意寻找
senses.example: I observed a crack in the glass before it fell.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃掉落之前，我就注意到上面有道裂痕。
senses.why: Attention can be caught as well as directed, so the same verb covers the moment something enters the eye.
senses.whyCN: 注意力既能被引导也能被抓住，因此同一个动词也覆盖某物进入视野的那一刻。

senses.title: To measure in a study
senses.definition: to record a phenomenon under controlled conditions as part of scientific work
senses.definitionCN: 作为科研工作的一部分，在受控条件下记录一种现象
senses.example: The team observe the cells every six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 团队每六小时观察一次这些细胞。
senses.why: Measurement begins with watching, and science made the watching formal by giving it conditions and records.
senses.whyCN: 测量始于观看，而科学通过附加条件与记录，把观看变得正式。

senses.title: To remark
senses.definition: to say something as a comment on what has been noticed
senses.definitionCN: 就注意到的事情说一句话作为评论
senses.example: The reviewer observed that the sample was too small.
senses.exampleCN: 评审人评论说样本太小。
senses.why: A remark is often the spoken form of something noticed, so the verb moved from the eye to the mouth.
senses.whyCN: 评论常常是「注意到的东西」的口头形式，这个动词于是从眼睛移到了嘴。

senses.title: To keep a rule
senses.definition: to act in accordance with a law, rule, custom or promise
senses.definitionCN: 依照法律、规则、习俗或承诺行事
senses.example: Drivers must observe the speed limit near the school.
senses.exampleCN: 司机在学校附近必须遵守限速。
senses.why: To observe a rule is to keep watch over yourself, the same inward attention the Latin verb first described.
senses.whyCN: 遵守规则就是看住自己，正是那个拉丁动词最初描述的内在注意。

senses.title: To mark a day or rite
senses.definition: to celebrate or carry out a day, festival or ceremony in the proper way
senses.definitionCN: 以适当方式庆祝某个日子、节日或举行仪式
senses.example: The village observes the harvest festival every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子每年秋天都过丰收节。
senses.why: A custom is kept by being performed on its day, so the sense of keeping widened to the act of celebration.
senses.whyCN: 习俗靠在其日子被践行而得以保持，因此「持守」之义扩展到庆祝行为。

senses.title: To keep someone under watch
senses.definition: to watch a person or place secretly, especially as part of an investigation
senses.definitionCN: 暗中监视某人或某地，尤作为调查的一部分
senses.example: Police observe the house from a van across the street.
senses.exampleCN: 警察在街对面的货车里监视那栋房子。
senses.why: The same careful watching turns into surveillance when the watcher does not wish to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 当观看者不愿被看见，同样的仔细观看就变成了监视。

senses.title: To watch without interfering
senses.definition: in research, to study behaviour while taking no part that would change it
senses.definitionCN: 在研究中研究行为，同时不介入以免改变它
senses.example: The psychologist observes the class from the back of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学家在教室后排观察这个班。
senses.why: If the observer changes what is observed, the record is spoiled, so method demands watching with hands off.
senses.whyCN: 观察者若改变了被观察对象，记录就毁了，因此方法要求袖手旁观。

intro.en: Observe comes from Latin observare 'to watch over, heed', built on ob- 'over, before' and servare 'to keep, preserve'. The rule-keeping and celebration senses came through religious usage, and the scientific sense settled in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: observe 来自拉丁语 observare「看守、留心」，由 ob-「在……之上、在……之前」与 servare「保持、守护」构成。守规与庆祝两义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义则在十七世纪定型。

items.en: Servare meant to keep safe, preserve or watch over, and it stands behind preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.cn: servare 意为保全、守护、看守，preserve、reserve 与 conserve 都出自它。

items.en: The similar-looking servire meant to serve, and it gave servant and service; the two Latin verbs are different words.
items.cn: 形近的 servire 意为服侍，产生了 servant 与 service；这两个拉丁动词是不同的词。

items.en: Ob- plus servare made a verb for watching over something and attending to it, with attention as the core.
items.cn: ob- 加 servare 构成「看守并留心某物」的动词，核心在注意。

items.en: Old French observer carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of keeping a rule.
items.cn: 古法语 observer 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，最初意为遵守规则。

items.en: Observing the Sabbath and observing a fast fixed the senses of keeping a custom and of celebrating its day.
items.cn: 守安息日、守斋期固定了「持守习俗」与「在其日子举行」两种含义。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy made observe a technical word for recorded watching, and observatory and observer followed.
items.cn: 十七世纪的天文学把 observe 变成指「有记录观看」的技术词，天文台与观察者二词随之而来。

note.en: The first group shares the keeping root or looks close; the second group names ways of watching.
note.cn: 第一组共享「守护」词根或形近；第二组是各种「看」的方式。

entries.definition: The act or result of watching and recording.
entries.definitionCN: 观看并记录的行为或结果。

entries.definition: The person who watches, including the mere onlooker.
entries.definitionCN: 进行观看的人，也包括单纯旁观者。

entries.definition: Quick to notice details; also careful in keeping rules.
entries.definitionCN: 善于察觉细节的；也指守规谨慎的。

entries.definition: The keeping of a rule or rite, not the act of looking.
entries.definitionCN: 对规则或仪式的遵行，而非观看动作。

entries.definition: A building fitted for watching the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 为观测天空而建的场所。

entries.definition: To keep safe from harm, from the same keeping verb with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 使免受损害，同一守护动词加不同前缀。

entries.definition: Work done for others, from servire 'to serve', not from servare.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人所做的工作，出自表示「服侍」的拉丁动词，而非表示「守护」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for looking at something over a period, with less formality.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指持续一段时间看某物，正式程度较低。

entries.definition: To become aware of something, without the suggestion of sustained study.
entries.definitionCN: 意识到某物，不含持续研究的意味。

entries.definition: To keep a continuous check, often with instruments.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查，常借助仪器。

entries.definition: To look over a whole area or group, often to record its state.
entries.definitionCN: 遍览整个区域或群体，常为记录其状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the keeping verb, the real family and the fixed phrases of rules, rites and research.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「守护」动词、真实同族词，以及规则、仪式与研究里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin servare meant to keep safe, so observe is literally to keep watch over something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 servare 意为保全，observe 字面就是看住某物。

normal.en: The family runs observe, observation, observer, observant and observatory.
normal.cn: 同族词有 observe、observation、observer、observant 与 observatory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: observe a rule, observe a holiday, observe that.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：遵守规则、庆祝节日、评论说。

normal.en: Preserve and reserve share the keeping verb, while servant and service come from the serving verb.
normal.cn: preserve 与 reserve 共享「守护」动词，而 servant 与 service 出自「服侍」动词。

normal.en: An observatory is a building named for the watching, not for the stars.
normal.cn: 天文台是因「观看」而得名，而非因星星。

abstract.en: To observe a rule is to watch yourself as closely as you watch others.
abstract.cn: 遵守规则，就是像看别人那样看住自己。

abstract.en: The observer who changes the scene has already lost the thing worth recording.
abstract.cn: 改变场景的观察者，已经失去了值得记录的东西。

abstract.en: Attention is the whole word: watch, keep, and do not blink.
abstract.cn: 整个词就是注意：看着、守着、别眨眼。

examples.en: She observed the birds from the hide without making a sound.
examples.cn: 她藏在小棚里观察鸟，没有发出一点声音。

examples.en: Every driver must observe the signs at the crossing.
examples.cn: 每位司机在路口都必须遵守标志。

examples.en: The committee observed a minute of silence for the victims.
examples.cn: 委员会为遇难者默哀一分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「欧布泽夫」——守在旁边盯住不放，看到什么就记下来：观察

root: 拉丁语 servare「保全、守护」→ observare「看守、留心」（ob- 加 servare）；经古法语 observer 进入英语。守规与庆祝义经宗教用法而来，科学观测义在十七世纪定型。注意与 servire「服侍」并非同词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pair of watching eyes: sustained attention, a sudden notice, a measured record, a spoken remark, a rule kept, a festival marked, a house watched in secret, and a class studied without interference.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一双观看的眼睛：持续注意、忽然察觉、有记录的测量、口头评论、被遵守的规则、被举行的节日、被暗中监视的房子，以及不干预地研究的课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: on a hilltop a watcher holds a telescope on one star and writes its position every quarter hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：山顶的观测者用望远镜对准一颗星，每刻钟记下它的位置。

branches.en: THE EYES: watching for a long time, and catching something in passing.
branches.cn: 那双眼：长时间的看，与路过时捕捉到什么。

branches.en: THE RECORD: cells counted every six hours, a class watched from the back without interference.
branches.cn: 记录：每六小时数一次细胞，在教室后排不干预地观察一个班。

branches.en: THE MOUTH: a note spoken aloud after the eyes have done their work.
branches.cn: 嘴：眼睛做完活之后，说出口的一句评论。

branches.en: THE KEPT RULE: attention turned inward, so that the driver watches himself.
branches.cn: 被守的规则：注意转向内部，司机看住自己。

branches.en: THE MARKED DAY AND THE SECRET WATCH: a rite performed on its date, a house watched from a van.
branches.cn: 被举行的日子与暗中监视：在正日子举行的仪式，与从货车里盯住的房子。

intro.en: Observe is a Latin verb of keeping watch, and its family split off from the separate verb meaning to serve.
intro.cn: observe 是一个表示看守的拉丁动词，其词族与另一个意为服侍的动词分道而行。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is servare, ob-, observare and the noun observatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 servare、ob-、observare 与名词 observatio。

items.example: The verb keeps the image of a guard at a post.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留着岗哨看守的意象。

items.example: It also gives preserve, reserve and conserve.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「保存」「保留」与「保护」三词的来源。

items.example: It gives servant and service, and is not the root here.
items.exampleCN: 它产生「仆人」与「服务」两词，不是这里的词根。

items.example: It adds the idea of watching over something.
items.exampleCN: 它加上「看住某物」的意思。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The noun names both the act and its record.
items.exampleCN: 名词兼指行为与其记录。

items.example: The agent noun includes the mere onlooker.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词包括单纯旁观者。

items.example: The adjective also means careful in keeping rules.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也指守规谨慎的。

items.meaning: the keeping of a rule or rite
items.example: It names practice, not perception.
items.exampleCN: 它命名实践，而非感知。

items.example: The suffix names a place of work.
items.exampleCN: 词尾命名工作场所。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb servare (serv-, servatum; to keep)
latinEntries.example: Latin servare means to keep or preserve.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 servare 意为保持、守护。

latinEntries.example: Latin ob- appears in obicere, to throw against.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ob- 见于 obicere（扔向对面）。

latinEntries.example: Latin observare means to watch over, to heed.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observare 意为看守、留意。

latinEntries.example: Latin observatio means a watching or a noting.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 observatio 意为观看、记录。

definition_zh: 物理学；物理；（口语）事物的物理特性与运作原理
definition_en: the science of matter, energy, motion and the forces that govern them, or the physical way something works
core_image: 一只摆锤从最高点落下，旁边并排放着温度计、磁铁与棱镜，都在量同一件事：物体如何运动与相互作用
scene: 实验室里，学生记录单摆周期、测量透镜焦距，试图用同一条定律解释两种现象。 In the laboratory students timed a pendulum and measured the focal length of a lens, hoping that one law of physics would explain both.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究物质、运动与相互作用的物理学」，对应第 1 个义项：作为一门学科的整体；句意为学生用同一条物理定律解释单摆与透镜两种现象。画面要点：摆锤、温度计、磁铁、棱镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 物理学（不可数，作学科名称；口语中也可指某物的运作机制）

derivatives.zh: 物理的；身体的（希腊语中表示「自然」的词加形容词后缀，指属于物质世界的，后也指人的身体）
在物理上；身体上（形容词加副词后缀，指从物质或身体的角度）
物理学家（学科名词加表从事者的后缀，指以物理学为专业的人）
天体物理（表示「星体」的前缀与物理学复合，指用物理方法研究天体）
形而上学（表示「之后、超越」的前缀与物理学复合，原指编在物理学之后的讨论，后指研究存在本身的学问）

senses.title: The science of matter and motion
senses.titleCN: 研究物质与运动的学科
senses.definition: the branch of science that studies matter, energy, motion, forces and the structure of the universe
senses.definitionCN: 研究物质、能量、运动、力以及宇宙结构的那门科学
senses.example: In the laboratory students timed a pendulum and measured the focal length of a lens, hoping that one law of physics would explain both.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室里，学生记录单摆周期、测量透镜焦距，希望同一条物理定律能解释两者。
senses.why: The Greek source named 'natural things', so the discipline begins as the study of whatever happens by nature rather than by human arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为「自然之物」，因此这门学科起初研究的是依本性而非依人造安排发生的一切。

senses.title: How a particular thing works
senses.titleCN: 某具体事物的运作原理
senses.definition: the physical principles behind a device, a sport or a natural event
senses.definitionCN: 某个装置、某项运动或某种自然现象背后的物理原理
senses.example: The coach explained the physics of a spinning ball.
senses.exampleCN: 教练讲解了旋转球的物理原理。
senses.why: The name of a whole discipline can be applied to one small case, because every case is an instance of the same laws.
senses.whyCN: 整门学科的名称可以用在一个小案例上，因为每个案例都是同一批定律的实例。

senses.title: Classical mechanics in practice
senses.definition: the part of the subject dealing with bodies moving well below the speed of light, as formulated before relativity
senses.definitionCN: 研究远低于光速运动的物体、在相对论之前已成体系的那部分内容
senses.example: The bridge design was checked with classical physics.
senses.exampleCN: 桥梁设计用经典物理作了校核。
senses.why: The old core of the subject kept the plain name, so 'physics' often means the mechanics of ordinary speeds and sizes.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科旧有的核心保留了这个朴素的名字，因此「物理」常指日常速度与尺度下的力学。

senses.title: Relativity and the quantum
senses.titleCN: 相对论与量子层面的现代物理
senses.definition: the parts of the subject that describe very fast, very massive or very small systems
senses.definitionCN: 描述极快、极重或极小系统的那部分内容
senses.example: Modern physics begins where the classical laws stop working.
senses.exampleCN: 现代物理从经典定律失效之处开始。
senses.why: When the old laws failed at the extremes, the same word had to cover the theories that replaced them.
senses.whyCN: 当旧定律在极端情形下失效，同一个词就必须覆盖取而代之的新理论。

senses.title: Branch subjects built on the name
senses.titleCN: 以该词构成的各分支学科
senses.definition: fields formed by joining a prefix to the subject, such as the physics of stars, of the earth or of living things
senses.definitionCN: 在学科名称前加前缀构成的领域，如研究星体、地球或生物的那几门
senses.example: Astrophysics applies the methods of physics to stars.
senses.exampleCN: 天体物理把物理学的方法用于星体。
senses.why: A method that works on one scale invites use on every scale, so the name becomes a suffix for whole new fields.
senses.whyCN: 在一个尺度上有效的方法会被用到所有尺度，于是这个名字成了新领域的后缀。

senses.title: A course and a textbook
senses.titleCN: 一门课程与一本教科书
senses.definition: the school or university subject as it is taught, examined and written up
senses.definitionCN: 在学校或大学里被教授、考核与编写成书的那门科目
senses.example: She took physics in her first year and chemistry in her second.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一年修物理，第二年修化学。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a subject when it acquires a syllabus, and the same noun then names the room, the hour and the book.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问获得教学大纲后就成了科目，同一个名词于是也命名教室、课时与课本。

senses.title: The mechanism behind an outcome
senses.definition: the practical cause-and-effect chain that makes something happen, used in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 使某事发生的实际因果链条，用于日常口语
senses.example: The physics of the market is not the same as the physics of a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市场的运作机制与桥梁的运作机制并不相同。
senses.why: Speakers borrow the word whenever they want to say that something has a mechanism rather than a mystery.
senses.whyCN: 说话者借用这个词，是想说某事有一套机制，而不是一个谜。

senses.title: Natural philosophy in older use
senses.definition: the older name for the study of nature, before the modern sciences separated
senses.definitionCN: 现代各门科学分化之前，研究自然的学问的旧称
senses.example: Newton wrote his great work under the old name for physics.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿以物理学的旧称写下他的巨著。
senses.why: Before disciplines divided, the study of nature was one subject, and its old title is still visible in the word's ancestry.
senses.whyCN: 在各学科分化之前，对自然的研究是一门学问，它的旧称仍可见于这个词的来历。

intro.en: Physics comes from Greek phusis 'nature', through Latin physica 'natural things'. English first used physic for medicine, and later took physics for natural science, so the two forms parted company.
intro.cn: physics 出自希腊语 phusis「自然」，经由拉丁语 physica「自然之物」传入。英语先用 physic 指医学，后来用 physics 指自然科学，两种形式从此分道。

items.en: Phuein 'to grow, bring forth' is the verb at the root of the family, and it describes what comes into being by itself.
items.cn: phuein 意为「生长、产生」，是这个词族的根动词，描述自行生成之物。

items.en: Phusis 'nature' named the way things grow and behave on their own, as opposed to what is made by craft.
items.cn: phusis 意为「自然」，指事物自行生长与表现的方式，与人以技艺造作之物相对。

items.en: Ta phusika 'natural things' was the title of Aristotle's treatises on nature, and the phrase became the name of the subject.
items.cn: ta phusika 意为「自然之物」，是亚里士多德论自然诸篇的标题，这个说法后来成为学科名称。

items.en: Latin physica, a neuter plural, named natural science, and it passed into English in that form.
items.cn: 拉丁语 physica 是中性复数，指自然科学，并以这一形式进入英语。

items.en: In English physic first meant the art of healing, because medicine studied the natural body; that sense survives in the word for a doctor.
items.cn: 在英语中，physic 起初指医术，因为医学研究的是自然身体；这一意思残留在表示医生的那个词里。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the plural form was used for natural science, while the singular stayed with medicine. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，复数形式用来指自然科学，单数形式则留在医学。年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek word for nature but has split into medicine, body build and the adjective; the second group places the subject among neighbouring sciences.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语中表示「自然」的词，但已分成医学、体格与形容词；第二组把这门学科放进相邻的科学之中。

entries.definition: The art of healing, now archaic; it is the same source word, but it named medicine rather than the science of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 医术，现已古旧；它是同一个来源词，但命名的是医学，而不是研究物质的科学。

entries.definition: The shape and strength of a person's body; it comes from the same Greek root but through French, and names a frame rather than a field.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身体的形态与力量；它出自同一希腊词根，但经法语传入，命名的是体格而不是学科。

entries.definition: Of matter or the body, as opposed to the mental; it describes a kind of thing, while the entry word names a science.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的或身体的，与心理的相对；它描述一类事物，而本词命名一门科学。

entries.definition: A person trained in the subject; the suffix marks the practitioner rather than the field.
entries.definitionCN: 受过该学科训练的人；后缀标示从业者，而不是领域。

entries.definition: Any science of the physical world, including biology, chemistry and geology; the entry word is one member of it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物理世界的任何科学，包括生物学、化学与地质学；本词是其中一员。

entries.definition: The study of bodies and the forces acting on them; it is a branch of the entry subject rather than a synonym for it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究物体及作用其上的力；它是本学科的一个分支，而不是同义词。

entries.definition: Sciences of non-living systems, such as physics and chemistry; the phrase is broader and excludes biology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究非生命系统的科学，如物理与化学；这个说法更宽，但不包括生物学。

entries.definition: Organised knowledge obtained by observation and experiment; it covers every discipline, of which the entry word is one.
entries.definitionCN: 经观察与实验获得的系统知识；它覆盖所有学科，本词是其中之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Greek word for nature, the Latin plural for natural things, real derived words and real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：希腊语中表示「自然」的词、拉丁语中表示「自然之物」的复数、真实派生词与真实分支名称。

normal.en: The root means nature, so the subject begins as the study of what happens by itself.
normal.cn: 词根意为「自然」，因此这门学科起初研究自行发生之事。

normal.en: The family runs physical, physically, physicist, astrophysics and metaphysics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括物理的、身体上、物理学家、天体物理与形而上学。

normal.en: The older singular meant medicine, which is why a doctor and a scientist share a root.
normal.cn: 较早的单数形式指医学，所以医生与科学家共有一个词根。

normal.en: The subject splits into classical and modern halves, and into branches named by a prefix.
normal.cn: 这门学科分成经典与现代两半，也分成由前缀命名的各分支。

normal.en: A pendulum and a lens obey the same laws, which is the promise the word makes.
normal.cn: 单摆与透镜服从同一批定律，这正是这个词所许诺的事。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum at the top of its arc, a thermometer beside it and a prism splitting light, all waiting to be measured.
abstract.cn: 想象一只摆锤停在弧线的最高点，旁边是温度计，还有一块分光的棱镜，都在等着被测量。

abstract.en: Picture a single law written on a card, held up against two completely different experiments.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡片上写着一条定律，被举到两组完全不同的实验面前。

abstract.en: Picture a tree whose trunk is nature and whose branches are named after stars, rocks and living cells.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树，树干是「自然」，枝干则以星体、岩石与活细胞命名。

examples.en: The physics of the atmosphere explains why the balloon rose so fast.
examples.cn: 大气的物理原理解释了气球为何上升得那么快。

examples.en: He studied physics before turning to the history of science.
examples.cn: 他先修物理，后来转向科学史。

examples.en: No law of physics forbids the machine, only the cost does.
examples.cn: 没有物理定律禁止这台机器，只是成本不允许。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费兹克斯」——「费」力气去「测」：摆锤、棱镜、温度计，量的都是同一件事，这就是物理。

root: 希腊语 phuein「生长、产生」→ phusis「自然」→ ta phusika「自然之物」→ 拉丁语 physica「自然科学」→ 英语 physics。较早的英语形式 physic 指医学，后复数形式专指自然科学；这一分开的年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings radiate from one discipline. The subject itself comes first, then the practical physics of a single thing, then its classical core, its modern extensions, its branch subjects, its life as a course, its looser use for any mechanism, and its older name as natural philosophy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一门学科辐射开。先是学科本身，其次是某件具体事物的运作原理，再其次是它的经典内核、现代扩展、各分支学科、作为课程的存在、泛指任何机制的宽松用法，以及它作为「自然之学」的旧名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a swinging pendulum beside instruments that all measure the same interaction.
core.cn: 核心意象：摆动的摆锤，旁边是一同测量同一种相互作用的仪器。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: the whole discipline, and the same thing as a course and a textbook.
branches.cn: 学科：整体学问，以及它作为课程与教科书的存在。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM: how one thing works, and the everyday use of the word for any causal chain.
branches.cn: 机制：某物如何运作，以及日常口语中用这个词泛指任何因果链。

branches.en: CLASSICAL CORE: bodies at ordinary speeds, governed by the older laws.
branches.cn: 经典内核：日常速度下的物体，由较早的定律支配。

branches.en: MODERN EDGE: what happens at extreme speed, mass or smallness.
branches.cn: 现代边缘：在极端速度、质量或微小尺度下发生的事。

branches.en: BRANCHES AND ANCESTOR: prefix-named fields, and the older single study of nature.
branches.cn: 分支与祖先：以前缀命名的各领域，以及较早的那门统一的自然之学。

intro.en: The family comes from a Greek verb for growing, through a Greek noun for nature and a Latin plural for natural things; English then built adjectives, persons and whole branch names on it.
intro.cn: 这个词族出自一个表示「生长」的希腊动词，经由表示「自然」的希腊名词与表示「自然之物」的拉丁复数，英语再在其上构成形容词、人物名词与整批分支名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below are themselves borrowed from Greek; they carried the subject into English and also left the older word for medicine.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式本身借自希腊语；它们把这门学科带入英语，也留下了表示医学的那个较早的词。

items.meaning: the science of matter and motion
items.meaningCN: 研究物质与运动的科学
items.example: Physics explains why the apple falls.
items.exampleCN: 物理学的解释了苹果为何下落。

items.example: The physical world obeys measurable laws.
items.exampleCN: 物质世界服从可测量的定律。

items.example: The task is physically demanding.
items.exampleCN: 这项任务对体力要求很高。

items.example: The physicist measured the decay rate.
items.exampleCN: 那位物理学家测量了衰变率。

items.meaning: the art of healing, now archaic
items.example: The old physic book lists herbal remedies.
items.exampleCN: 那本旧医书列着草药方。

items.meaning: the physics of stars and space
items.meaningCN: 研究星体与太空的物理
items.example: Astrophysics studies how stars form.
items.exampleCN: 天体物理研究恒星如何形成。

items.example: Geophysics maps the rock beneath the city.
items.exampleCN: 地球物理测绘城市地下的岩层。

items.example: Biophysics models how proteins fold.
items.exampleCN: 生物物理为蛋白质折叠建立模型。

items.meaning: the study of being, placed after the physical treatises
items.meaningCN: 研究存在的学问，原编排在物理诸篇之后
items.example: The question belongs to metaphysics, not to physics.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题属于形而上学，而不是物理学。

latinEntries.structure: physica, physicorum (n., neuter plural, from Greek)

derivatives.zh: 物理的；身体的（希腊语中表示「自然」的词加形容词后缀，指属于物质世界的，后也指人的身体）
在物理上；身体上（形容词加副词后缀，指从物质或身体的角度）
物理学家（学科名词加表从事者的后缀，指以物理学为专业的人）
天体物理（表示「星体」的前缀与物理学复合，指用物理方法研究天体）

definition_zh: 股息；红利；被除数；回报
definition_en: a share of profit paid to shareholders, or a number to be divided
core_image: 一只钱袋被分成几小袋，递给持有股份的人
scene: 公司年报公布后，董事会决定把更多利润以现金分给持股人。 The board raised the dividend after a strong year.
sceneCN: 这里指「分给股东的利润」，对应第 1 个义项：公司从利润中按股份支付给股东的款项；句意为业绩强劲的一年后，董事会提高了股息。画面要点：年报、钱袋、股东名单。

pos.zh: 股息；红利；被除数；回报；保单红利

senses.title: A share of profit paid to shareholders
senses.definition: a part of a company's profit distributed to its shareholders
senses.definitionCN: 公司利润中分给股东的一部分
senses.example: The company pays a dividend twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司每年派发两次股息。
senses.why: The word literally means that which is to be divided: profit is cut into portions and one portion goes to each share.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上指「应当被分掉的东西」：利润被切成几份，每份股份得一份。

senses.title: An interim or final payment
senses.titleCN: 期中或期末派发的股息
senses.definition: a dividend paid at a scheduled point in the financial year
senses.definitionCN: 在财年某个既定节点支付的股息
senses.example: The interim dividend rose to eight cents.
senses.exampleCN: 期中股息升至八分。
senses.why: The same share of profit is named by its timing, since a payment can be made halfway through the year or at its close.
senses.whyCN: 同一份利润按支付时点得名，因为款项可以在年中或年末支付。

senses.title: A benefit from an action
senses.definition: an advantage or return that results from effort or investment
senses.definitionCN: 由努力或投入产生的益处或回报
senses.example: The training paid dividends in fewer accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项培训在减少事故上带来了回报。
senses.why: Profit is abstracted from money to any good result, so an effort can be said to pay dividends even without shares.
senses.whyCN: 利润从金钱抽象为任何好结果，所以即使没有股份，一项努力也能说带来回报。

senses.title: A number to be divided
senses.definition: the number that is divided by another in arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 算术中被另一个数除的数
senses.example: In twelve divided by three, twelve is the dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 在十二除以三中，十二是被除数。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense: the quantity that is cut up by division, before finance borrowed the name.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面义：被除法切分的数量，金融后来借用了这个名字。

senses.title: An insurance policy dividend
senses.definition: a share of surplus returned to holders of certain insurance policies
senses.definitionCN: 某些保险保单持有人分得的盈余份额
senses.example: The mutual insurer returned a dividend to policyholders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家互助保险公司向保单持有人返还了红利。
senses.why: An insurer's surplus is divided among the people who funded it, so the profit-share sense moves from shares to policies.
senses.whyCN: 保险公司的盈余在出资人之间分配，利润份额义于是从股份转到保单。

senses.title: A cooperative patronage dividend
senses.titleCN: 合作社按交易量分配的盈余
senses.definition: a share of a cooperative's surplus returned according to members' trade
senses.definitionCN: 合作社按成员交易额返还的盈余份额
senses.example: The farmers' cooperative paid a patronage dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 农民合作社支付了按交易额计算的盈余。
senses.why: Cooperative members are owners and customers at once, so surplus is divided by how much each used the business.
senses.whyCN: 合作社成员同时是所有者与顾客，所以盈余按各人使用企业的多少来分。

senses.title: A dividend paid in shares
senses.definition: a distribution made by issuing additional shares instead of cash
senses.definitionCN: 通过增发股份而非现金进行的分配
senses.example: The company chose a stock dividend to keep cash.
senses.exampleCN: 公司选择股票股利以保留现金。
senses.why: The portion is still divided out, but the portion consists of new shares rather than money.
senses.whyCN: 分出去的仍然是份额，只是这一份由新股份而不是现金构成。

senses.title: A dividend paid in cash
senses.definition: a distribution paid directly in money
senses.definitionCN: 直接以金钱支付的分配
senses.example: Investors prefer a steady cash dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者偏好稳定的现金股息。
senses.why: This is the plainest financial reading: profit is divided and the holder receives money rather than paper.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的金融读法：利润被分开，持有人收到的是钱而不是纸。

intro.en: Dividend comes from a Latin gerundive meaning that which is to be divided; the arithmetic sense is older than the financial one. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dividend 出自拉丁语动形词，意为「应当被分掉的东西」；算术义早于金融义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dividere meant to force apart, cleave or distribute; it is generally analysed as dis- 'apart' plus a second element meaning to separate, though the deeper origin of that element is source uncertain.
items.cn: dividere 意为分开、劈开、分配；一般分析为 dis-「分开」加一个表示「分离」的成分，但该成分更深的来源不确定。

items.en: The gerundive dividendum meant that which is to be divided, a form used in arithmetic and in sharing out amounts.
items.cn: 动形词 dividendum 意为「应当被分掉的东西」，用于算术与分配数额。

items.en: English arithmetic books used dividend for the number to be divided, the sense that still survives in mathematics.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语算术书用 dividend 指被除数，这一义项至今留在数学中。

items.en: Joint-stock companies began to divide surplus profit among shareholders and called each portion a dividend.
items.cn: 合股公司开始把剩余利润分给股东，并把每一份称为 dividend。

items.en: Insurance, cooperatives and stock-based payments extended the word to policyholders, members and shares issued instead of cash.
items.cn: 保险、合作社与以股代现的支付方式，把这个词扩展到保单持有人、合作社成员与增发股份。

note.en: The first group is built on the same dividing root and is easily confused; the second group names other kinds of payment or return.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「分开」的词根上，容易混淆；第二组是其他类型的支付或回报。

entries.definition: The number by which another is divided; the dividend is above the line, the divisor below it.
entries.definitionCN: 用来除另一个数的数；被除数在除号上方，除数在下方。

entries.definition: The act or operation of dividing; it is the process, while a dividend is one of the quantities involved.
entries.definitionCN: 划分或除的动作；它是过程，而 dividend 是参与其中的一个量。

entries.definition: To separate or share out; the verb names the action that produces a dividend.
entries.definitionCN: 分开或分配；动词表示产生股息或被除数的动作。

entries.definition: A single person, literally one that cannot be divided; it shares the root but has no sense of a portion paid out.
entries.definitionCN: 单个的人，字面是「不可再分者」；共享词根，但没有分出份额的意思。

entries.definition: A sum of money paid out, from insurance, gambling or a company; it is broader than dividend.
entries.definitionCN: 从保险、博彩或公司付出的款项；比股息更宽泛。

entries.definition: The formal sharing out of money or assets; a dividend is one kind of distribution.
entries.definitionCN: 对金钱或资产的正式分配；股息是分配的一种。

entries.definition: An extra payment, often discretionary; a dividend follows ownership, while a bonus often follows performance.
entries.definitionCN: 额外支付的款项，常出于酌情；股息跟随所有权，奖金常跟随业绩。

entries.definition: The total gain from an investment, including interest and price change; a dividend is only one part of a return.
entries.definitionCN: 投资的总收益，包括利息与价格变化；股息只是回报的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin meaning that which is to be divided, real fixed phrases and real arithmetic relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语「应当被分掉者」、真实固定搭配与真实算术同族词。

normal.en: The word is the thing to be divided, which explains both the arithmetic and the financial senses.
normal.cn: 这个词就是「要被分掉的东西」，这同时解释了算术义与金融义。

normal.en: Profit is cut into portions, and each share receives one portion.
normal.cn: 利润被切成几份，每一股得到其中一份。

normal.en: Insurance surplus and cooperative surplus are divided the same way among the people who funded them.
normal.cn: 保险盈余与合作社盈余也按同样方式在出资人之间分配。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the finance sense: dividend yield, cash dividend, stock dividend.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出金融义：股息收益率、现金股息、股票股利。

normal.en: The phrase pay dividends keeps the metaphor alive: effort is an investment that can return a portion.
normal.cn: 「产生回报」这一说法保留了比喻：努力是一项能返回一份的投资。

abstract.en: Picture a money bag opened and its contents split into small bags for the people who own the company.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱袋被打开，里面的钱分成小袋，交给拥有公司的人。

abstract.en: Picture the same splitting action drawn as a number above a line, waiting to be divided.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个分配动作画成横线上方的一个数，等待被除。

abstract.en: Picture a seed of effort later opening into several small bags of benefit.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒努力的种子后来裂开成几小袋好处。

examples.en: Shareholders approved the higher dividend at the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 股东们在年度会议上批准了更高的股息。

examples.en: Patience with the new process paid dividends within a year.
examples.cn: 对新流程的耐心在一年内带来了回报。

examples.en: In the expression forty divided by eight, forty is the dividend.
examples.cn: 在四十除以八这个算式中，四十是被除数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「利润被分成小份」——每一股拿一份 → 股息；算式里被除的那个数 → 被除数

root: 拉丁语 dividere「分开、分配」的动形词 dividendum「应当被分掉的东西」；先用于算术的被除数，十七世纪起用于分给股东的利润份额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all depend on division: a profit is cut into portions, a scheduled payment is named by its timing, the benefit spreads beyond money, and arithmetic keeps the oldest literal sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都依赖「分开」：利润被切成几份，按支付时点得名，好处超出金钱，而算术保留了最古老的字面义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a money bag split into small bags for the people who own the company.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只钱袋被分成小袋，交给拥有公司的人。

branches.en: CORE SHARE: profit is divided, and one portion follows each share.
branches.cn: 核心份额：利润被分开，每一股跟随一份。

branches.en: FORMS OF PAYMENT: the same portion can be interim or final, paid in cash or issued as shares.
branches.cn: 支付形式：同一份可以是期中或期末，以现金支付或以股份发放。

branches.en: BENEFIT: the divided portion becomes any good result that effort returns.
branches.cn: 好处：被分出的份额变成努力返回的任何好结果。

branches.en: ARITHMETIC: the quantity that is to be divided keeps the oldest literal meaning.
branches.cn: 算术：应当被除的那个量保留了最古老的字面义。

branches.en: OTHER SURPLUS: insurers and cooperatives divide surplus among policyholders and members.
branches.cn: 其他盈余：保险公司与合作社在保单持有人与成员之间分配盈余。

intro.en: Dividend belongs to the Latin family of dividere, whose pieces still appear in English words about separation and arithmetic.
intro.cn: dividend 属于拉丁语 dividere 一族，其成分仍出现在表示分离与算术的英语词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin dividere 'to divide' gives divide, division, divisor and individual, literally one who cannot be divided.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dividere「分开」衍生 divide、division、divisor 与 individual，后者字面是「不可再分者」。

items.example: The prefix marks separation.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标示分离。

items.example: The stem appears in divide and division.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干出现在划分与除法等词里。

items.meaning: that which is to be done
items.meaningCN: 应当被做的（动形词词尾）
items.example: The ending marks something due to be acted on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标示应当被处理的对象。

items.example: They divided the land equally.
items.exampleCN: 他们把土地平分。

items.meaning: the act of dividing, or a part formed by it
items.meaningCN: 划分动作，或由此形成的部分
items.example: The division of labour raised output.
items.exampleCN: 分工提高了产量。

items.meaning: a portion of profit, or a number to be divided
items.example: The dividend was paid in June.
items.exampleCN: 股息在六月支付。

items.example: Dividends rose for three years.

items.meaning: the number by which one divides
items.example: Eight is the divisor in this sum.
items.exampleCN: 在这个算式里八是除数。

items.example: Ten is divisible by five.

items.example: The proposal proved divisive.

definition_zh: 物质；事情；问题；要紧、有关系；【医】脓液
definition_en: the physical stuff that things are made of, an affair under discussion, or to be important
core_image: 一块被雨水泡软的黑泥，手指一捏就能变形，也能弄脏任何碰到它的东西
scene: 泥地刚被雨水浸透，脚一踩就陷下去，鞋底带起黏稠的一团。 The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 matter 指构成物体的有形之物（第 1 个义项：与形式相对、可被感官触及的实体材料）；句意：那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。图中可辨识物件：泥洼、沾泥的靴子、铁锹、水桶；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 物质；事情；问题；脓液
要紧；有重大关系

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 就事论事的；不动声色的（由本词与「事实」一词构成的复合形容词）
反物质（加表示「相反」的前缀构成，指电荷相反的物质）
无实质内容的（加表示「没有」的后缀构成）
含脓的（加形容词后缀构成，旧医学用法，现已罕用）

senses.title: Physical substance
senses.definition: the physical substance that occupies space and can be seen or touched
senses.definitionCN: 占据空间、可被看见或摸到的实体材料
senses.example: The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。
senses.why: matter goes back to Latin materia, which meant timber and the stuff a thing is built from, so the physical sense is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: matter 上溯到拉丁 materia，本指木料与造物所用的料，因此「有形之物」是最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: An affair or business
senses.titleCN: 一件待办或已办的事情
senses.definition: a situation, event or piece of business that someone deals with
senses.definitionCN: 某人需要处理的情境、事件或事务
senses.example: She settled a few private matters before leaving for the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 去海边之前，她先处理了几件私事。
senses.why: Latin materia also named the subject under discussion, so the stuff of a talk became the affair itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 materia 也指谈论的题目，于是「谈话的料」就变成了「事情本身」。

senses.title: A problem to be solved
senses.titleCN: 出了差错、需要弄清的问题
senses.definition: a trouble or difficulty, especially one whose cause is not yet known
senses.definitionCN: 麻烦或困难，尤指原因尚未查明的那一种
senses.example: The mechanic asked what the matter was with the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工问发动机出了什么毛病。
senses.why: an affair that has gone wrong is still an affair, so the same word shifted from business to trouble.
senses.whyCN: 出了岔子的事情仍然是一件事情，这个词便从「事务」滑到「麻烦」。

senses.title: To be important
senses.definition: to be of importance or consequence to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事具有重要性或后果
senses.example: Accuracy matters more than speed in this laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 在这间实验室里，准确比速度更要紧。
senses.why: what has substance has weight, and English turned that picture into the verb sense of counting for something.
senses.whyCN: 有实体就有分量，英语把这个画面变成了「算得上数」的动词义。

senses.title: The topic of a text or talk
senses.definition: the subject or content that a piece of writing, speech or study is about
senses.definitionCN: 一篇文章、一段讲话或一项研究所谈论的主题与内容
senses.example: The matter of the lecture was soil chemistry in dry regions.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座的主题是干旱地区的土壤化学。
senses.why: the material of a text is what it carries, and that carrying sense became the topic it treats.
senses.whyCN: 文章的「料」就是它所承载的东西，这一承载义再转为它所处理的主题。

senses.title: Grounds for concern
senses.titleCN: 值得忧虑或申诉的根据
senses.definition: a reason or grounds for a feeling, claim or action
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪、主张或行动的根据与理由
senses.example: The inspectors found matter for concern in the water samples.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员在采水样中发现了值得忧虑的情况。
senses.why: a matter is something that exists and can be pointed at, so it came to mean a fact solid enough to base a claim on.
senses.whyCN: 事情是存在且指得出的事物，于是引申为「站得住脚、可作依据的事实」。

senses.title: Pus from a wound
senses.definition: the fluid that forms in an infected wound, formerly called matter
senses.definitionCN: 感染伤口中生成的液体，旧时称作 matter
senses.example: The old surgical notes describe the wound discharging matter.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手术记录描述伤口流出脓液。
senses.why: early medicine used matter for any fluid substance of the body, and pus was simply the matter a wound produced.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学用 matter 泛指体内各种液体，脓不过是伤口生成的「物质」。

senses.title: Content as opposed to form
senses.titleCN: 与形式相对的实质内容
senses.definition: the substantive content of a work, as distinct from its style or outward form
senses.definitionCN: 作品的实际内容，与风格或外在形式相对
senses.example: The matter of the essay outweighs its elegant phrasing.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇随笔的内容比它漂亮的措辞更有分量。
senses.why: philosophy opposed matter to form, and literary criticism then asked whether a work had matter behind its shape.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把「质料」与「形式」对举，文学批评随后追问一部作品在形之外有没有实质。

intro.en: Matter came into English through Old French from Latin materia 'timber, stuff, subject'. The common claim that materia derives from mater 'mother' is a hypothesis, not a settled derivation.
intro.cn: matter 经古法语来自拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」。常有人说 materia 由 mater「母亲」派生，那是假说，并非已定的词源。

items.en: Materia meant timber and the material a thing is made from, and by extension the subject of a discussion.
items.cn: materia 指木料以及造物所用的材料，引申为谈论的题目。

items.en: A widely repeated suggestion links materia to mater 'mother', as if the stuff were the mother of the object; this remains a hypothesis and is not established.
items.cn: 一种广为流传的说法把 materia 与 mater「母亲」联系起来，仿佛材料是器物的母亲；这仍属假说，未获证实。

items.en: Old French matere carried both the physical sense and the sense of a subject or affair into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 matere 在诺曼时期之后把「物质」与「题目、事务」两义一并带入英语。

items.en: Middle English matter already covered stuff, a business, a question and grounds for complaint, so the wide sense range is old, not modern.
items.cn: 中古英语的 matter 已兼指物质、事务、问题与申诉的理由，可见义域之宽古已有之，并非现代才有。

items.en: Medical writing of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries used matter for bodily fluid and especially for pus, a use that has since narrowed.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的医学文献用 matter 指体液，尤指脓，这一用法后来收窄。

items.en: The first recorded dates for several senses are approximate; the word itself is well attested from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 若干义项的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十三世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group contains forms that look or sound close to matter but may sit on a different root; the second group contains words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形或音与 matter 接近、但未必同源的词；第二组是与之部分同义的词。

entries.definition: Built on Latin materialis from materia, so it is the adjective and noun grown from the same stock as matter, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 materialis 构成，而 materialis 出自 materia，因此它是与 matter 同出一源的名词与形容词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: A French-shaped doublet of material, borrowed later for military equipment and supplies; it shares the Latin source but not the everyday meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 是 material 的法语式借形词，后借入指军用装备与物资；与 material 同源，但日常义不同。

entries.definition: From Latin mater 'mother' through maternellus; it is related to mater, and only through the unproven mater-materia hypothesis could it be called a cousin of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 经 maternellus 出自拉丁 mater「母亲」；它与 mater 有关，只有借助尚未证实的「母亲—材料」假说，才能算作 matter 的远亲。

entries.definition: From Latin matrix 'womb, mould', built on mater; it names a mould or grid, and does not descend from materia.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 matrix「子宫、模具」，由 mater 构成；它指模具或网格，并非由 materia 传下。

entries.definition: Physical stuff considered as what stands under qualities; matter stresses the material, substance stresses independent existence.
entries.definitionCN: 把物质看作承载属性的基底；matter 强调材料，substance 强调独立存在。

entries.definition: A matter of business or public concern; it covers only the affair sense and never the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 指事务或公众关注之事；只覆盖「事务」义，绝不指物质。

entries.definition: A topic on which people disagree; it is narrower than matter because it always implies debate.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们有分歧的议题；比 matter 窄，因为它总含争辩之意。

entries.definition: The everyday word for unspecified material; matter is its neutral and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指未指明材料的日常说法；matter 是它中性、技术化的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin materia first meant timber, so matter is the stuff a thing is built from.
normal.cn: 拉丁 materia 最初指木料，因此 matter 就是造物所用的料。

normal.en: The family runs matter, material, materially, immaterial and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 matter、material、materially、immaterial 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the affair sense: a matter of time, as a matter of fact, no matter what.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「事情」义：只是时间问题、事实上、无论发生什么。

normal.en: Subject matter keeps the topic sense visible in publishing and teaching.
normal.cn: 「主题素材」这一说法让「主题」义在出版与教学里一直可见。

normal.en: The verb is used in questions of value: it matters, it does not matter.
normal.cn: 动词义出现在价值判断里：这要紧、这不要紧。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay that takes the shape of whatever presses into it.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土，什么按上去就留下什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with one folded note on it, and everyone asks about that note first.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上只有一张折起的字条，所有人先问的都是那张字条。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the pan with real goods sinks and the empty pan rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，装了实物的那端沉下去，空的那端翘起来。

examples.en: In legal drafting, the matter of a contract means its operative content rather than its layout.
examples.cn: 在法律起草中，合同的 matter 指其有效内容，而不是排版。

examples.en: Dark matter does not emit light, yet its gravity holds galaxies together.
examples.cn: 暗物质不发光，但它的引力把星系维系在一起。

examples.en: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as the measurements stay exact.
examples.cn: 只要测量保持精确，你走得多慢都不要紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈特」——妈妈特别在意的那件事，就是要紧的事 → 事情、要紧；妈妈捏的那团泥，就是物质

root: 拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」（一说由 mater「母亲」派生，仅为常见假说）→ 古法语 matere「材料、事务」→ 英语 matter；「问题」与「脓」义由「事情」「体内物质」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one lump of stuff: it is the material of things, then the material of talk, then the affair, the trouble inside it, the fact that carries weight, the topic of a text, the fluid in a wound, and finally content set against form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一团「料」辐射出去：先是造物的材料，再是谈话的材料，继而成为事情、事情里的麻烦、有分量的事实、文本的主题、伤口的液体，最后是与形式相对的实质内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of wet clay that can be shaped, weighed and pointed at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团湿黏土，可被塑形、称重、指认。

branches.en: THE LUMP ITSELF: clay in the yard and pus in a wound are both stuff a body or a boot meets.
branches.cn: 这团东西本身：院里的泥与伤口的脓，都是身体或靴子会碰到的实体。

branches.en: THE AFFAIR AND ITS SNAG: business first, then the trouble discovered inside it.
branches.cn: 事情与其中的疙瘩：先是事务，再是事务里查出的麻烦。

branches.en: WEIGHT THAT COUNTS: what has substance can tip a decision, so matter becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 有分量才算数：有实体就能压动决定，于是 matter 变成动词。

branches.en: STUFF POINTED AT: the material of a text turns into its topic, and a solid fact into grounds.
branches.cn: 被指认的料：文本的材料变成主题，扎实的事实变成依据。

branches.en: CONTENT AGAINST FORM: philosophy keeps the lump as what remains when style is stripped away.
branches.cn: 内容对形式：哲学把那团料保留为剥去风格后剩下的东西。

intro.en: Matter is built on a Latin root that also yields material and immaterial, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: matter 建立在一个拉丁词根上，同一词根还生出 material 与 immaterial，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia supplies matter, material and materialis; mater supplies maternal and matrix, with the materia link remaining a hypothesis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material 一系；mater 衍生 maternal 与 matrix 一系，而 materia 与 mater 的联系仍属假说。

items.example: The root gives the picture of stuff a thing is built from.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「造物所用之料」的画面。

items.example: Its link to materia is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.exampleCN: 它与 materia 的联系只是假说，并非已证的派生。

items.example: The adjective suffix turns stuff into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀把「料」变成描述性的词。

items.example: Material keeps both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: It also shapes editorial and commercial.
items.exampleCN: 它同样构成 editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The negation covers both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: The plan materialized as a real building.
items.exampleCN: 计划落实成了一座真实的建筑。

items.example: The later borrowing narrowed to army supplies.
items.exampleCN: 后借入的这一形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 植物学家；研究植物的专家
definition_en: a person who studies plants scientifically, or who collects, identifies, and classifies them
core_image: 一个人蹲在草丛里，用放大镜看花蕊，笔记本上写满拉丁学名
scene: 温室里，植物学家把花瓣一片片摊平。 In the glasshouse, the botanist used tweezers to take a stamen and wrote the family, genus, species, and collection number in her notebook.
sceneCN: 这里 botanist 是「植物学家」（第 1 个义项：以研究植物为专业的人）；句意：温室里，植物学家用镊子取下一枚花蕊，在记录本上写下科、属、种和采集编号。场景要点：镊子、花蕊、记录本、拉丁学名、采集编号、温室植株。

pos.zh: 植物学家；植物学工作者

collocations.zh: 经济植物学家（研究有用植物）
这位植物学家的采集品

derivatives.zh: 植物学上；从植物学角度
采集植物；进行植物考察

senses.title: A scientist who studies plants
senses.definition: a person who studies plants as a profession, usually with formal training in botany
senses.definitionCN: 以研究植物为职业的人，通常受过正式的植物学训练
senses.example: She became a botanist after finishing her doctorate on alpine mosses.
senses.exampleCN: 她完成关于高山苔藓的博士研究后成为植物学家。
senses.why: Botanist is botan- plus -ist, the agent suffix. The stem names the field and -ist names the person, so the word begins as 'one who practises botany' rather than as a description of a quality.
senses.whyCN: botanist 是 botan- 加施动后缀 -ist。词干命名领域，-ist 命名人，因此这个词的起点是“从事植物学的人”，而不是描述某种性质。

senses.title: Field botanist: the collector outdoors
senses.titleCN: 野外植物学家：在户外采集的人
senses.definition: a botanist who works in the field, finding, pressing, and recording plants where they grow
senses.definitionCN: 在野外工作的植物学家，在植物生长地寻找、压制并记录植物
senses.example: A field botanist spent three weeks surveying the valley's orchids.
senses.exampleCN: 一位野外植物学家花了三周调查这个山谷的兰科植物。
senses.why: The suffix identifies the person, while 'field' identifies where the practice happens. Collecting is the oldest form of the job: the specimen comes before the theory, so the agent noun is narrowed by its workplace.
senses.whyCN: 后缀标识人，field 标识实践发生的地点。采集是这份工作最古老的形式：标本先于理论，因此这个施动名词被工作场所所收窄。

senses.title: Taxonomist: the namer and classifier
senses.titleCN: 分类学家：命名与归类的人
senses.definition: a botanist who describes, names, and places plants in the taxonomic system
senses.definitionCN: 描述、命名并把植物放入分类系统的植物学家
senses.example: The botanist published a revision of the genus in a taxonomic journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这位植物学家在分类学期刊上发表了对该属的修订。
senses.why: Naming is the part of botany that turns a plant into a retrievable record. A taxonomic botanist is therefore the keeper of the Latin labels, a role rather than a new word.
senses.whyCN: 命名是把植物变成可检索记录的那部分植物学。因此分类植物学家就是拉丁标签的保管人；这是一种角色，而不是另一个新词。

senses.title: Specialist branches of the profession
senses.definition: a botanist may also be a plant physiologist, ecologist, geneticist, or molecular botanist, depending on the layer of the plant studied
senses.definitionCN: 植物学家也可以是植物生理学家、生态学家、遗传学家或分子植物学家，取决于研究植物的哪一层
senses.example: A molecular botanist studies the genes that control flowering time.
senses.exampleCN: 一位分子植物学家研究控制开花时间的基因。
senses.why: The same agent noun covers every subfield because all of them study plants. The modifier names the layer of study, not a different kind of person, so the core sense stays intact.
senses.whyCN: 同一个施动名词覆盖所有子领域，因为它们都在研究植物。修饰语命名的是研究层次，而不是另一种人，因此核心义保持不变。

senses.title: Historical: herbalist and plant collector
senses.titleCN: 历史义：草药师与植物采集者
senses.definition: before botany became a university science, a botanist was often a herbalist or an amateur collector of medicinal plants
senses.definitionCN: 在植物学成为大学科学之前，botanist 常指草药师或采集药用植物的业余爱好者
senses.example: In the 17th century a botanist might keep both a herb garden and a dried collection.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪，一位 botanist 可能既经营药草园，又保存干燥标本。
senses.why: The word is recorded from the 17th century, when plant knowledge was still tied to medicine. The modern professional sense grew out of that older practical role, so the agent noun widened before it narrowed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从 17 世纪起有记录，当时植物知识仍与医药相连。现代的职业义正是从那更早的实用角色中长出来的：这个施动名词先变宽，后又收窄。

senses.title: Applied botanists outside academia
senses.titleCN: 学术界之外的应用植物学家
senses.definition: a botanist employed in agriculture, forestry, conservation, or industry, applying plant science to practical problems
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于农业、林业、保护或工业，把植物科学用于实际问题的植物学家
senses.example: An economic botanist searches for wild relatives of crop plants.
senses.exampleCN: 一位经济植物学家寻找农作物的野生近缘种。
senses.why: The suffix says what the person knows, not where they work. Applied fields therefore use the same noun and add a modifier for the sector, which is how the profession extends beyond the university.
senses.whyCN: 后缀说明这个人懂什么，而不是在哪里工作。因此应用领域用同一个名词，只添加标明行业的修饰语；职业范围就这样延伸到大学之外。

senses.title: Everyday: the knowledgeable plant lover
senses.titleCN: 日常用法：懂植物的爱好者
senses.definition: in informal use, a very knowledgeable plant enthusiast may be called a botanist, though not a professional one
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中，非常懂植物的爱好者也可被称为 botanist，但并非职业人士
senses.example: My neighbour is a botanist of sorts; she can name every weed in the lane.
senses.exampleCN: 我邻居算得上半个植物学家，巷子里每种野草她都叫得出名字。
senses.why: The word can be used loosely because the boundary of the profession is knowledge, not a licence. The hedge 'of sorts' keeps the informal use honest while borrowing the prestige of the agent noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以宽松使用，因为这一职业的边界是知识，而不是执照。of sorts 这样的限定语让非正式用法保持诚实，同时借用了这个施动名词的声望。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanist versus horticulturist
senses.definition: a botanist studies plants; a horticulturist grows and cultivates them for gardens, food, or sale
senses.definitionCN: botanist 研究植物；horticulturist 为园艺、食用或销售而栽培植物
senses.example: The botanist identified the species; the horticulturist worked out how to propagate it.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家鉴定了物种；园艺师则研究出如何繁殖它。
senses.why: Both work with plants, but one produces knowledge and the other produces plants. The suffixes differ as -ist of a science versus -ist of a cultivation practice, so the two agent nouns are not interchangeable.
senses.whyCN: 两者都跟植物打交道，但一个产出知识，另一个产出植株。后缀同样都是 -ist，区别在于一个是科学，一个是栽培实践，因此两个施动名词不能互换。

senses.title: Usage boundary: botanist versus biologist
senses.definition: a botanist is a kind of biologist; biologist is the wider term for anyone who studies living things
senses.definitionCN: botanist 是 biologist 的一种；biologist 是研究生物者的更宽泛称呼
senses.example: As a biologist she works on fungi; as a botanist she would have to exclude them.
senses.exampleCN: 作为生物学家她研究真菌；若作为植物学家，她就得把真菌排除在外。
senses.why: The stem restricts the field to plants, while -ist only marks the practitioner. Botanist is therefore narrower than biologist, not a synonym of it, because the stem does the restricting.
senses.whyCN: 词干把领域限制在植物，而 -ist 只标记从业者。因此 botanist 比 biologist 窄，不是它的同义词，收窄工作由词干完成。

intro.en: Botanist is the same stem as botany with a different suffix: botan- names the field and -ist names the person. The stem is Greek in origin and reached English through medieval Latin; the suffix is a general agent ending, not a plant word. The recorded dates for botanist and botany are slightly inconsistent, so the exact order of formation is uncertain.
intro.cn: botanist 与 botany 词干相同，后缀不同：botan- 命名领域，-ist 命名人。词干源自希腊语，经中世纪拉丁语进入英语；后缀是一般的施动者词尾，本身不是植物词。botanist 与 botany 的记录年代略有矛盾，因此确切的构词先后存疑。

items.en: Greek botanē meant 'plant, grass, pasture, fodder', and botanikos meant 'of herbs'. Etymonline notes that these words seem to have more to do with pasturage than with plant science; related forms include botamia 'pastures' and boter 'herdsman'. The deeper origin of the family is not established.
items.cn: 希腊语 botanē 意为“植物、草、牧场、牧草”，botanikos 意为“草本的”。etymonline 指出这些词更多与放牧有关，而非与植物科学有关；相关形式有 botamia“牧场”、boter“牧人”。这个词族的更深来源尚未确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin botanicus 'of plants' carried the Greek adjective into learned Latin, and French botanique (17c.) passed the same stem into English as botanic.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 botanicus“植物的”把这个希腊形容词带入学术拉丁语，法语 botanique（17 世纪）又把同一词干以 botanic 的形式传入英语。

items.en: English botanic is recorded from the 1650s, botany from the 1690s, and botanist from the 1680s. Etymonline derives botany from botanic, adding -y on the model of astronomy, and botanist from botany + -ist. The dates leave botanist apparently earlier than botany; that contradiction means the exact derivation order is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 botanic 于 17 世纪 50 年代有记录，botany 于 17 世纪 90 年代有记录，botanist 于 17 世纪 80 年代有记录。etymonline 认为 botany 来自 botanic，仿 astronomy 加 -y；botanist 来自 botany + -ist。这些年代使 botanist 表面上早于 botany；这一矛盾说明确切的派生先后存疑。

items.en: -ist comes from Greek -istēs through Latin -ista and French -iste. It is built from the stem ending of verbs in -izein plus the agent suffix -tēs, and it forms nouns meaning 'one who practises or believes', as in artist, scientist, and botanist. It adds no plant meaning of its own.
items.cn: -ist 经拉丁语 -ista、法语 -iste 上溯希腊语 -istēs。它由 -izein 动词词干的结尾加施动后缀 -tēs 构成，形成表示“从事者或信奉者”的名词，如 artist、scientist、botanist。它本身不添加任何植物含义。

items.en: Herbaria, overseas expeditions, and Linnaean taxonomy turned plant study into a paid profession. Botanist then settled into its modern sense of a trained plant scientist, while the older overlap with herbalists and gardeners faded. The exact period of this shift is not fixed.
items.cn: 标本馆、海外考察与林奈分类学把植物研究变成有薪职业。botanist 由此固定为“受过训练的植物科学家”这一现代义，而与草药师、园艺者的旧重叠逐渐消退。这一转变的确切时期并无定论。

items.en: Modern usage adds modifiers for molecular, ecological, and conservation specialties but keeps one noun. The word stays narrower than biologist because its stem names plants, not life in general.
items.cn: 现代用法为分子、生态与保护等方向添加修饰语，却保留同一个名词。由于词干命名的是植物而非一切生命，这个词始终比 biologist 窄。

note.en: The first group is the same botan- stem with three different endings; the second separates the plant scientist from the gardener, the herbalist, the ecologist, and the wider life scientist.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个 botan- 词干配三种不同后缀；第二组把植物学家与园艺者、草药师、生态学家及更宽泛的生命科学家区分开。

entries.definition: The science of plants. It is the field itself, while botanist is the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究植物的科学。它是学科本身，而 botanist 是从事这门学科的人。

entries.definition: Relating to plants or botany. It describes a quality or relation, while botanist names a person.
entries.definitionCN: 植物的；植物学的。它描述性质或关系，而 botanist 命名人。

entries.definition: In botanical terms; from the viewpoint of plant science. The -ly ending makes it modify a verb or statement, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 从植物学角度；以植物学的说法。-ly 结尾使它修饰动词或陈述，而不是人。

entries.definition: To collect or study plants in the field. The -ize suffix turns the field into an activity, so it names what a botanist does, not who they are.
entries.definitionCN: 在野外采集或研究植物。-ize 后缀把学科变成活动，因此它命名植物学家做什么，而不是他们是谁。

entries.definition: A person who studies living things. Botanist is a narrower kind of biologist, limited to plants.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物的人。botanist 是 biologist 中较窄的一类，限于植物。

entries.definition: A person who grows and cultivates plants for gardens, food, or sale. The focus is on producing plants, not on producing knowledge about them.
entries.definitionCN: 为园艺、食用或销售而栽培植物的人。重点在产出植株，而不是产出关于植物的知识。

entries.definition: A person who uses plants as medicine, often in a traditional practice. Botanist studies plants scientifically rather than treating patients with them.
entries.definitionCN: 用植物治病、常从事传统实践的人。botanist 以科学方式研究植物，而不是用植物治疗病人。

entries.definition: A person who studies how organisms relate to their environment. A botanist may study a plant's ecology, but the ecologist's unit is the whole system.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与环境关系的人。植物学家可能研究某种植物的生态，但生态学家的单位是整个系统。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the agent suffix -ist, the field noun botany, and the working verbs botanize and botanically describe.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：施动后缀 -ist、学科名词 botany，以及实际使用的动词 botanize 与副词 botanically。

normal.en: botany + -ist = botanist: the field first, the person second. The suffix adds 'one who practises', not 'plant'.
normal.cn: botany + -ist = botanist：先有学科，再有人。后缀添加的是“从事者”，不是“植物”。

normal.en: The -ist in botanist is the same -ist as in artist and scientist: a person who does the work.
normal.cn: botanist 里的 -ist 与 artist、scientist 里的 -ist 相同：做这项工作的人。

normal.en: A field botanist carries a press and a notebook; the specimen is the first document of the science.
normal.cn: 野外植物学家带着标本夹和记录本；标本是这门科学的第一份文档。

normal.en: A taxonomic botanist owns the Latin names: genus and species are the addresses that make a plant findable.
normal.cn: 分类植物学家掌管拉丁名：属与种是让植物可被找到的地址。

normal.en: Botanist is narrower than biologist because botan- names plants, while bio- names life in general.
normal.cn: botanist 比 biologist 窄，因为 botan- 命名植物，而 bio- 命名一般生命。

abstract.en: A person bent over a flower with a lens: the whole profession is the act of looking closely and writing down what is seen.
abstract.cn: 一个人俯身用放大镜看花：整个职业就是靠近观察并把所见写下来。

abstract.en: A herbarium sheet is a passport: the plant travels through time because someone signed it with a Latin name.
abstract.cn: 一份腊叶标本就是一本护照：因为有人在上面签了拉丁名，这株植物得以穿越时间。

abstract.en: The botanist stands between the wild plant and the written record, turning a living thing into a repeatable observation.
abstract.cn: 植物学家站在野生植物与书面记录之间，把一个活物变成可重复的观察。

examples.en: The botanist spent the morning pressing specimens for the herbarium.
examples.cn: 这位植物学家花了一上午为标本馆压制标本。

examples.en: A botanist and a horticulturist worked together to save the rare orchid.
examples.cn: 一位植物学家和一位园艺师合作拯救这种稀有兰花。

examples.en: As a botanist, she is careful to distinguish mosses from lichens.
examples.cn: 作为植物学家，她谨慎地把苔藓与地衣区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: “博坦尼斯特”——博物（博）学家在园里蹲（tan）下，拿着放大镜研究植物 → botanist 植物学家

root: botan-（植物、牧草，希腊 botanē / botanikos，经中世纪拉丁语 botanicus 入英语）+ -ist（施动后缀，希腊 -istēs，经拉丁 -ista、法语 -iste）；-ist 表示从业者，不表示植物。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of botanist all name the same person from different angles: a trained plant scientist, a field collector, a namer, a specialist, a historical herbalist, an applied worker, a keen amateur, and two boundary cases.
sensesIntro.cn: botanist 的九个义项从不同角度命名同一种人：受过训练的植物科学家、野外采集者、命名者、专门方向研究者、历史中的草药师、应用工作者、热心的业余爱好者，以及两个边界情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who looks closely at plants, collects them, and turns them into named records.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人靠近观察植物、采集它们，并把它们变成有名字的记录。

branches.en: CORE: the agent noun itself, 'one who practises botany'.
branches.cn: 核心：施动名词本身，即“从事植物学的人”。

branches.en: FIELD AND NAME: collecting outdoors and naming in the herbarium are the two oldest halves of the job.
branches.cn: 野外与命名：户外采集与标本馆命名，是这份工作最古老的两半。

branches.en: SPECIALTY AND APPLICATION: the same noun takes modifiers for the layer studied or the sector worked in.
branches.cn: 专门方向与应用：同一个名词接受修饰语，标明研究层次或工作行业。

branches.en: HISTORY AND EVERYDAY: the old herbalist role and the knowledgeable amateur both stretch the word beyond the licensed profession.
branches.cn: 历史与日常：旧时的草药师角色与懂行的业余爱好者，都把词义拉到执照职业之外。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES: horticulturist produces plants, biologist studies all life; botanist sits between them.
branches.cn: 边界：horticulturist 产出植株，biologist 研究一切生命；botanist 位于两者之间。

intro.en: Botanist has one live suffix, -ist, on a borrowed Greek stem. The suffix is productive and can be added to other fields, while botan- stays fixed and supplies the plant meaning.
intro.cn: botanist 在借来的希腊词干上只有一个活后缀 -ist。这个后缀能产，可加在其他领域上；botan- 则固定不变，提供植物义。

latinIntro.en: The botan- stem is Greek, carried into English through Medieval Latin botanicus and French botanique. The agent suffix -ist also has a Latin stage, -ista, before it reached French and English.
latinIntro.cn: botan- 词干是希腊语，经中世纪拉丁语 botanicus 与法语 botanique 进入英语。施动后缀 -ist 也有拉丁阶段 -ista，之后才到法语和英语。

items.meaning: a person who studies plants; the shift is from a field to its practitioner
items.meaningCN: 研究植物的人；语义从学科转到从业者
items.example: The botanist recorded the plant's habitat and date.
items.exampleCN: 这位植物学家记录了该植物的生境与日期。

items.structure: botan- + -y (name of a field, on the model of astronomy)
items.meaning: the science of plants; the noun that supplies the profession's field
items.meaningCN: 植物学；为这一职业提供学科名的名词
items.example: Botany and zoology were once taught together as natural history.
items.exampleCN: 植物学与动物学曾作为博物学一起教授。

items.meaning: pertaining to plants; the shorter adjective
items.meaningCN: 植物的；较短的那个形容词
items.example: The botanic garden dates from the eighteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这座植物园可追溯到 18 世纪。

items.meaning: relating to plants or botany; the default adjective
items.meaningCN: 植物的；植物学的；默认形容词
items.example: The botanical description notes the leaf's hairs and veins.
items.exampleCN: 植物学描述记录了叶片的毛被与叶脉。

items.example: Botanically, the tomato is a berry.
items.exampleCN: 从植物学上说，番茄是一种浆果。

items.structure: botan- + -ize (to act in a particular way)
items.meaning: to collect or study plants in the field
items.meaningCN: 在野外采集或研究植物
items.example: They botanized the coastal dunes at low tide.
items.exampleCN: 他们在退潮时考察了海岸沙丘的植物。

items.meaning: a person who studies how a culture uses plants
items.meaningCN: 研究某一文化如何使用植物的人
items.example: An ethnobotanist documented the village's medicinal plants.
items.exampleCN: 一位民族植物学家记录了该村的药用植物。

items.meaning: a person who studies fossil plants
items.example: The paleobotanist identified a fern from the Jurassic.
items.exampleCN: 这位古植物学家鉴定出一株侏罗纪蕨类。

items.meaning: the activity of collecting or studying plants in the field
items.meaningCN: 野外采集或研究植物的活动
items.example: A morning of botanizing produced forty pressed specimens.
items.exampleCN: 一个上午的植物考察采得四十份压制标本。

latinEntries.meaning: relating to plants; the source of the English stem
latinEntries.meaningCN: 与植物有关的；英语词干的来源

latinEntries.meaning: agent suffix 'one who practises'; the ancestor of English -ist
latinEntries.meaningCN: 施动后缀“从事者”；英语 -ist 的前身

senses.title: The shrinking variety of life
senses.definition: the decrease in the variety of living organisms in a place or on the planet
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区或全球范围内生物种类与差异性的减少
senses.example: Scientists warn that biodiversity loss is accelerating as forests are cleared.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家警告，随着森林被砍伐，生物多样性丧失正在加速。
senses.why: biodiversity names the variety itself, and loss names its going away, so the phrase reads literally as variety slipping out of existence.
senses.whyCN: biodiversity 指多样性本身，loss 指它消失，因此这个短语字面上就是「多样性正在消失」。

senses.title: Species richness falling
senses.titleCN: 物种丰富度下降（可测量义）
senses.definition: the measured drop in the number of species present in a habitat
senses.definitionCN: 某一生境中出现的物种数量可测的减少
senses.example: Repeated surveys recorded biodiversity loss of nearly a third.
senses.exampleCN: 重复调查记录到近三分之一的生物多样性丧失。
senses.why: once ecologists began counting species, the phrase acquired a number, and this countable reading is the one used in field reports.
senses.whyCN: 当生态学家开始统计物种数量，这个短语就有了数字，野外报告用的正是这一可测量的读法。

senses.title: Genetic variety eroded
senses.definition: the loss of genetic variation within a species, which leaves it less able to adapt
senses.definitionCN: 某一物种内部遗传变异减少，使其适应能力下降
senses.example: Isolated herds suffer biodiversity loss at the level of genes.
senses.exampleCN: 隔离的兽群在基因层面遭受生物多样性丧失。
senses.why: variety exists below the species level too, so the phrase extends downward from species to alleles.
senses.whyCN: 多样性也存在于物种层级之下，因此这个短语从物种向下延伸到等位基因。

senses.title: Habitats and ecosystems disappearing
senses.titleCN: 生态系统与生境类型的减少
senses.definition: the loss of different kinds of habitat or ecosystem across a region
senses.definitionCN: 一个区域内不同生境或生态系统类型的消失
senses.example: Draining the marshes meant biodiversity loss at the scale of whole habitats.
senses.exampleCN: 排干沼泽意味着整个生境层面的生物多样性丧失。
senses.why: ecologists count variety at three scales, and the largest scale is the ecosystem, so the phrase covers vanished habitat types as well.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家在三个尺度上统计多样性，最大尺度是生态系统，因此这个短语也涵盖消失的生境类型。

senses.title: A slide toward mass extinction
senses.definition: the worldwide decline of life measured against the background rate of extinction
senses.definitionCN: 以背景灭绝速率为参照衡量的全球生命衰退
senses.example: The living planet index is one way to track global biodiversity loss.
senses.exampleCN: 地球生命力指数是追踪全球生物多样性丧失的一种方式。
senses.why: when losses outpace new species, the phrase stops describing a place and starts describing a trajectory for the whole planet.
senses.whyCN: 当丧失速度超过新物种形成，这个短语就不再描述某地，而是描述整个行星的走向。

senses.title: The process driven by land conversion
senses.titleCN: 由开垦与占用驱动的过程义
senses.definition: the process by which farming, logging and settlement reduce the variety of life
senses.definitionCN: 农业、伐木与聚居使生命多样性下降的过程
senses.example: Agriculture is the leading driver of biodiversity loss worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 农业是全球生物多样性丧失的首要驱动因素。
senses.why: policy writing turns the state into an agent-driven process, so the phrase names what humans do as much as what disappears.
senses.whyCN: 政策文本把状态写成由主体驱动的过程，因此这个短语既指消失的东西，也指人所做的事。

senses.title: A term fixed by treaty
senses.titleCN: 条约与法律中的固定术语
senses.definition: the formal term used in treaties and statutes for the decline that states agree to stop
senses.definitionCN: 条约与法规中用来指各国同意遏止的下降的正式术语
senses.example: The 1992 convention put biodiversity loss on the legal agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 1992 年的公约把生物多样性丧失列入法律议程。
senses.why: a phrase becomes a term when a treaty needs a stable label for an obligation, and this is that label.
senses.whyCN: 当条约需要给一项义务一个稳定的名称，短语就变成术语，而这就是那个名称。

senses.title: Any measurable loss of variety
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何系统中多样性的减少
senses.definition: any measurable loss of variety in a system, not only in biology
senses.definitionCN: 任何系统中可测量的多样性减少，不限于生物
senses.example: Consolidating suppliers caused biodiversity loss in the supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 供应商合并导致供应链出现「生物多样性」式流失。
senses.why: the phrase is borrowed whenever a system is valued for its variety, so it can describe suppliers, dialects or crops.
senses.whyCN: 只要一个系统的价值在于其多样，这个短语就会被借用，因此可形容供应商、方言或作物。

intro.en: Biodiversity joins Greek bios 'life' to Latin diversus 'turned different ways', and was coined in the 1980s; loss is native English. The phrase itself is recent. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: biodiversity 把希腊 bios「生命」与拉丁 diversus「转向不同方向」并置，于 1980 年代被造出；loss 是英语本族词。整个短语出现很晚。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek bios meant 'life, way of life'. It entered modern scientific compounds through bio-, as in biology and biosphere.
items.cn: 希腊 bios 意为「生命、生活方式」，经 bio- 进入现代科学复合词，如 biology 与 biosphere。

items.en: Diversus, the past participle of divertere 'to turn in different directions', gave English diverse and diversity.
items.cn: diversus 是 divertere「转向不同方向」的过去分词，衍生英语 diverse 与 diversity。

items.en: The noun biodiversity is generally dated to the mid 1980s and is widely attributed to Walter G. Rosen; its spread followed a 1988 symposium volume edited by E. O. Wilson.
items.cn: 名词 biodiversity 一般认为是 1980 年代中期所造，广泛归功于 Walter G. Rosen；它的流行始于 1988 年由 E. O. Wilson 主编的会议文集。

items.en: Loss descends from Old English los 'destruction, loss', related to the verb lose; it is native Germanic stock, not Latin.
items.cn: loss 承自古英语 los「毁坏、丧失」，与动词 lose 相关，属本族日耳曼词，并非拉丁来源。

items.en: Biodiversity loss became a standard collocation in the 1990s, once the 1992 Convention on Biological Diversity made the decline a reporting obligation.
items.cn: 1990 年代，1992 年《生物多样性公约》把这一下降列为报告义务之后，biodiversity loss 成为标准搭配。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the exact first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded, the coinage date of biodiversity has minor competing accounts, and the deeper origin of Latin diversus is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：完整短语的最早印刷记录不明；biodiversity 的造词年代存在小的分歧说法；拉丁 diversus 的更深来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds terms built on the same bio- or diversity stock that are easily swapped; group two holds the neighbouring ideas that measure or describe the same decline.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 bio- 或 diversity 词干、容易被替换的术语；第二组是测量或描述同一衰退的邻近概念。

entries.definition: The variety itself. Biodiversity loss names what is happening to that variety, so the two cannot be swapped.
entries.definitionCN: 指多样性本身；biodiversity loss 指这种多样性正在遭遇什么，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: The longer academic wording for the same idea, older than biodiversity; it appears in treaty titles rather than in running text.
entries.definitionCN: 同一概念的较长学术说法，早于 biodiversity；多出现在条约标题中，而不用于行文。

entries.definition: The disappearance of habitat; it is one driver of biodiversity loss, not the loss of variety itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指生境消失；它是生物多样性丧失的驱动因素之一，而非多样性本身的减少。

entries.definition: The total disappearance of a species. Biodiversity loss is the broader decline that may end in extinctions.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个物种彻底消失；生物多样性丧失是可能以灭绝收场的那一更大范围衰退。

entries.definition: A drop in the numbers of one species; it does not by itself say anything about variety.
entries.definitionCN: 指单一物种数量的下降；本身不涉及多样性。

entries.definition: The weakening of an ecosystem's structure and function; biodiversity loss can follow from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指生态系统结构与功能退化；生物多样性丧失可能随之而来。

entries.definition: The loss of animal populations specifically; it leaves plants and microbes out of the count.
entries.definitionCN: 特指动物种群的丧失，不计植物与微生物。

entries.definition: A rhetorical term for life becoming poorer and fewer; it carries judgement that biodiversity loss as a metric does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指生命变得贫乏稀少的修辞说法；带有评价色彩，而作为指标的生物多样性丧失不带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bio- 'life' + diversity 'turned apart': the many kinds of life.
normal.cn: bio-「生命」+ diversity「转向不同」：生命种类的繁多。

normal.en: The family runs biodiversity, biological, diversity, diverse, loss, lose.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 biodiversity、biological、diversity、diverse、loss、lose。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: halt biodiversity loss, reverse biodiversity loss, global biodiversity loss.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义：遏止生物多样性丧失、扭转生物多样性丧失、全球生物多样性丧失。

normal.en: The phrase scales three ways: genes, species, ecosystems.
normal.cn: 这个短语有三个尺度：基因、物种、生态系统。

normal.en: Its usual drivers are habitat loss, overexploitation, invasive species, pollution and climate change.
normal.cn: 它的常见驱动因素是生境丧失、过度开发、入侵物种、污染与气候变化。

abstract.en: Picture a tree losing its leaves one shape at a time until the branches are bare.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树一种形状一种形状地掉叶子，直到枝条光秃。

abstract.en: Picture a choir where voices drop out until only one line is left singing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个合唱团，声部一个个退出，最后只剩一条声线在唱。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves empty by category, not by accident.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，书架按类别被清空，而非偶然散失。

examples.en: Biodiversity loss weakens the services that ecosystems provide to farms.
examples.cn: 生物多样性丧失削弱了生态系统为农田提供的服务。

examples.en: The report links biodiversity loss to the spread of new diseases.
examples.cn: 该报告把生物多样性丧失与新疾病的传播联系起来。

examples.en: Restoring hedgerows can slow local biodiversity loss.
examples.cn: 恢复树篱可以减缓局部的生物多样性丧失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「bio（生命）+ diversity（多样）+ loss（丢失）」——生命种类的多样在流失 → 生物多样性丧失

root: 希腊 bios「生命」（经 bio-）+ 拉丁 diversus「转向不同方向」（来自 divertere）+ 古英语 los「丧失」；biodiversity 为 1980 年代新造词，loss 为本族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one decline: variety goes missing, and the phrase is then scaled down to genes, up to ecosystems, out to the planet, and finally borrowed for any system valued for its variety.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一场衰退展开：多样性消失，这个短语再向下到基因、向上到生态系统、向外到整个行星，最后被借用于任何以多样为价值的系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree whose leaves fall one shape at a time until the branches show gaps.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵树的叶子一种形状一种形状地落，枝头露出空缺。

branches.en: GENERAL DECLINE: the plain reading, variety simply becoming less.
branches.cn: 总体下降：最朴素的读法，多样性就是变少了。

branches.en: COUNTED AND GENETIC: the drop is measured in species first, then inside the gene pool.
branches.cn: 可数层面与基因层面：先按物种计数，再深入基因库。

branches.en: HABITAT SCALE AND CAUSE: whole habitat types vanish, and land conversion is named as the driver.
branches.cn: 生境尺度与成因：整个生境类型消失，并把土地开垦列为驱动因素。

branches.en: PLANETARY TRAJECTORY: local losses add up to a slide toward mass extinction.
branches.cn: 行星走向：局部丧失累积成滑向大灭绝的趋势。

branches.en: TERM AND METAPHOR: treaty language fixes the label, and other systems borrow it.
branches.cn: 术语与隐喻：条约语言固定了名称，其他系统则借用它。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek life-prefix to a Latin noun of difference, then adds a native English noun of losing; it is a compound of free forms, not a root with suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊语的生命前缀接在拉丁语表示差异的名词上，再加一个英语本族表示丧失的名词；它是自由词形的复合，而非词根加后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin divertere gives diversity, diverse and divert; Greek bios supplies bio-, and Old English los supplies loss.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 divertere 衍生 diversity、diverse 与 divert；希腊 bios 提供 bio-，古英语 los 提供 loss。

items.structure: Greek bios (life) used as a combining form
items.example: Biology and biosphere both begin with this element.
items.exampleCN: biology 与 biosphere 都以这个成分开头。

items.example: The reef's diversity supports a huge food web.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁的多样性支撑起庞大的食物网。

items.example: The plot holds diverse grasses.
items.exampleCN: 这块地里有多种草。

items.example: The channel diverts flood water.
items.exampleCN: 这条渠道把洪水引开。

items.example: Biodiversity is highest near the equator.
items.exampleCN: 生物多样性在赤道附近最高。

items.example: Biodiversity loss is accelerating as forests are cleared.
items.exampleCN: 随着森林被砍伐，生物多样性丧失正在加速。

items.example: The loss of the marsh took a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽的消失用了十年。

items.example: The island lost half its birds.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛失去了一半的鸟类。

items.example: A lossy format throws away some detail.
items.exampleCN: 有损格式会丢掉一部分细节。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 转向不同方向的；多样的

definition_zh: 生物群系；生物群落区；大尺度生态系统类型
definition_en: a large ecological region characterized by its climate and the plant and animal communities that live there
core_image: 一张世界地图被划成十几块颜色不同的巨大区域，每块都标着典型植被
scene: 这里指「生物群系」。 The rainforest biome supports more species than any other region on land.
sceneCN: 这里 biome 指「生物群系」（第 1 个义项：由气候与植被界定的大尺度生态区域）；句意：雨林生物群系所支持的物种数超过任何其他陆地区域。图中可辨识物件：分区世界地图、雨林剖面、气候色带。

pos.zh: 生物群系；生物群落区；大尺度生态系统类型（可数，复数 biomes）

derivatives.zh: 微生物组（由 microbe 与 -ome 构成，与本词形近但所指不同）

senses.title: A Climate-Defined Region
senses.definition: a large region defined by its climate and its characteristic plant and animal communities
senses.definitionCN: 由气候及其典型动植物群落界定的大区域
senses.example: The rainforest biome supports more species than any other region on land.
senses.exampleCN: 雨林生物群系所支持的物种数超过任何其他陆地区域。
senses.why: Biome groups places that share a climate and therefore a way of life. It is a classification of regions, not a single place: every tropical rainforest on Earth belongs to one biome.
senses.whyCN: biome 把共享同一种气候、因而共享同一种生活方式的地区归到一起。它是对区域的分类，而不是某一地点：地球上每一片热带雨林都属于同一个生物群系。

senses.title: A Community in Place
senses.definition: the community of organisms occupying a particular region
senses.definitionCN: 占据某一特定区域的生物群落
senses.example: The island biome is cut off from the mainland by deep water.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的生物群落被深水与大陆隔开。
senses.why: The word can point to the living community of one area rather than to a global class. Geography decides which reading is meant, and 'the island biome' is clearly local.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指某一地区的生物群落，而不是全球性的类别；地理语境决定取哪一读法，而 the island biome 显然指局部。

senses.title: The Vegetation Belt
senses.titleCN: 植被带：气候对应的植被类型
senses.definition: a broad belt of vegetation determined by temperature and rainfall
senses.definitionCN: 由温度与降水决定的大片植被带
senses.example: Moving north, the biome changes from forest to tundra.
senses.exampleCN: 向北走，生物群系从森林变为苔原。
senses.why: Early ecologists described biomes mainly by their plants, because vegetation is what a traveller sees. Climate is the cause; the plant belt is the visible sign.
senses.whyCN: 早期生态学家主要按植物来描述生物群系，因为植被是旅行者看得见的东西；气候是原因，植被带是可见的标志。

senses.title: A Setting in a Game
senses.titleCN: 游戏中的生物群系：生成区域
senses.definition: a region type in a game or simulation, with its own terrain, plants and weather
senses.definitionCN: 游戏或模拟中具有特定地形、植被与天气的区域类型
senses.example: The game generates a new biome every few hundred metres.
senses.exampleCN: 游戏每几百米就生成一个新的生物群系。
senses.why: Games borrowed the word because their worlds are also divided by climate and vegetation. Here biome means a procedural region, a direct descendant of the ecological sense.
senses.whyCN: 游戏借用这个词，因为它们的虚拟世界也按气候与植被分区；此时 biome 指程序生成的区域，是生态义项的直接后代。

senses.title: A Unit of Mapping
senses.definition: a unit used to divide a territory into ecological zones
senses.definitionCN: 把一片地域划分为生态区域的单位
senses.example: Conservation plans are drawn at the biome scale.
senses.exampleCN: 保护规划是在生物群系的尺度上绘制的。
senses.why: Planners need units larger than a site and smaller than a planet. The biome fits that gap, which is why the word appears so often in conservation policy.
senses.whyCN: 规划者需要比单个地点大、比整个行星小的单位；biome 正好填上这个空档，因此在保护政策中频繁出现。

senses.title: The Ocean's Regions
senses.titleCN: 海洋生物群系：水体分区
