examples.en: The temple was regarded as the abode of the gods.
examples.cn: 这座神庙被视为众神的居所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额波德」——一盏灯、一把旧椅子，人在那儿一住多年，那间屋子就是住所。

root: 古英语 abad（停留），来自 abidan（停留、等待），再往前是日耳曼语 *bidan；核心义是「长期停留之处」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the act of staying to a home, then to permanent, animal, heavenly, temporary, figurative, and official dwellings.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从「停留」的行为走到家，再扩展到永久、动物、天上、临时、比喻与官方登记的居所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room where someone has long stayed
core.cn: 核心意象：有人长久停留的一间亮灯屋子

branches.en: A person's home, whether described by a writer or recorded by an office.
branches.cn: 人的家，或由作家描写，或由机构登记。

branches.en: The act or period of staying, including temporary lodging.
branches.cn: 停留的行为或时段，包括临时住处。

branches.en: An animal's shelter, where a creature makes its home.
branches.cn: 动物的庇护所，生物在那里安家。

branches.en: A sacred dwelling for gods or spirits.
branches.cn: 神灵或鬼魂的神圣居所。

branches.en: A figurative home for a quality such as learning or peace.
branches.cn: 学问或安宁等性质的比喻性居所。

intro.en: Abode is a native Germanic noun, so the useful pieces are the stem bod- and the endings that build the family from abide.
intro.cn: abode 是本土日耳曼语名词，因此有用的构件是词干 bod-，以及从 abide 构成词族的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Abode has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries are left empty rather than inventing a borrowed form.
latinIntro.cn: abode 没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁条目留空，而不编造借词形式。

definition_zh: 愿意服从的；顺从的；经得起检验的；有义务服从的
definition_en: willing to agree, cooperate, or submit to authority; open to testing or control
core_image: 温和低头的人：别人一提建议就点头配合
scene: 新来的实习生脾气很好，什么安排都乐意接受。 The new intern was amenable to every suggestion the manager made.
sceneCN: 这里的 amenable 是「愿意服从的、通情达理的」（第 1 个义项：乐于接受建议）；句意是这位新实习生对经理的每个建议都很乐意配合。

pos.zh: 愿服从的；通情达理的；肯合作的
经得起（检验、分析等）的

senses.title: Willing to cooperate or agree
senses.titleCN: 愿意配合的：乐于点头答应
senses.definition: open and responsive to suggestion; willing to agree or cooperate
senses.definitionCN: 对建议持开放态度，愿意同意或配合
senses.example: The landlord proved amenable to lowering the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东愿意配合降低租金。
senses.why: The Latin root minare means to drive animals with threats; a tame animal is one you can lead, hence a person you can persuade.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 minare 意为「驱赶牲畜」，温驯的牲畜可以牵走，由此引申为可以被说服的人。

senses.title: Responsible to a legal authority
senses.titleCN: 法律上须服从的：受管辖
senses.definition: liable to be brought under the jurisdiction or authority of a court or law
senses.definitionCN: 应受法院或法律管辖的，负服从义务的
senses.example: Foreign diplomats are amenable to local traffic laws in most countries.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数国家，外交官也须遵守当地交通法规。
senses.why: If a person can be 'led' by the law, the same herding image becomes legal obligation.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个人能被法律「牵引」，驱赶牲畜的意象就变成了法律义务。

senses.title: Open to testing or analysis
senses.titleCN: 经得起检验的：可供研究处理
senses.definition: capable of being tested, analyzed, or dealt with by a method
senses.definitionCN: 能够用某种方法加以检验、分析或处理的
senses.example: The data were amenable to statistical analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数据适合做统计分析。
senses.why: What willingly yields to a person also yields to a procedure; the word transfers to things.
senses.whyCN: 乐于向人让步的东西同样乐于向方法让步，词义由此转移到事物上。

senses.title: Responsive to medical treatment
senses.definition: responding favorably to medical treatment or therapy
senses.definitionCN: 对医疗或治疗产生良好反应的
senses.example: This cancer is highly amenable to radiation therapy.
senses.exampleCN: 这种癌症对放射治疗反应良好。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the sense of yielding: a disease that 'obeys' treatment is amenable.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「顺服」之义：肯「听话」的疾病就是对治疗有反应的疾病。

senses.title: Easily guided in temperament
senses.definition: having a mild, tractable disposition that others can guide
senses.definitionCN: 性情温和、容易被他人引导的
senses.example: Puppies that are amenable are much easier to train.
senses.exampleCN: 性情温顺的幼犬训练起来容易得多。
senses.why: The original image of driving livestock stays closest to the surface when we describe an animal's temperament.
senses.whyCN: 描述动物性情时，「驱赶牲畜」的本源意象最为贴近字面。

senses.title: Subject to rules or conditions
senses.definition: subject or subordinate to rules, conditions, or procedures
senses.definitionCN: 受规则、条件或程序约束的
senses.example: Membership benefits are amenable to the club's regulations.
senses.exampleCN: 会员权益须遵守俱乐部章程。
senses.why: Anything placed under a system is, figuratively, being led along that system's track.
senses.whyCN: 凡被纳入某个体系的事物，形象地说都是沿着该体系的轨道被牵引前行。

intro.en: Amenable traces to Anglo-French and medieval Latin words about leading animals, ultimately a metaphor for being led.
intro.cn: amenable 源自盎格鲁-法语和中世纪拉丁语中「驱赶牲畜」的词，最终是「被牵引」的隐喻。

items.en: Root *mei-, to move or drive, source of Latin minare.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *mei-「移动、驱赶」，是拉丁语 minare 的来源。

items.en: minare, to drive animals with cries or threats; minari, to threaten.
items.cn: 拉丁语 minare「以呼喝驱赶牲畜」；minari「威吓」。

items.en: aminare, to lead by threats; adjective aminabilis, liable to be led.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 aminare「以威吓牵引」，形容词 aminabilis「可被牵引的」。

items.en: amener, to lead or bring, from a- (to) plus mener (to lead).
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语 amener「引领、带来」，由 a-（向）+ mener（引导）构成。

items.en: English amenable first meant liable to be brought to account, then willing to be led.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 amenable 先指「应被追究责任」，后转为「愿意被引导」。

items.en: Now chiefly an agreeable, cooperative temperament or openness to treatment and analysis.
items.cn: 如今主要表示性格随和配合，或对治疗、分析持开放态度。

note.en: Do not confuse amenable with amendable or amenity; and pick near-synonyms carefully by register.
note.cn: 不要把 amenable 与 amendable、amenity 混淆；近义词也要按语域仔细区分。

entries.definition: able to be corrected or changed; from Latin emendare, not from minare.
entries.definitionCN: 可修正的、可修改的；源自拉丁语 emendare，与 amenable 词根不同，仅形近。

entries.definition: a pleasant feature or convenience; shares spelling start but a different branch of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 便利设施、宜人之处；拼写开头相似但词义分支不同，注意区分。

entries.definition: friendly and pleasant in manner; from Latin amare, to love — a different root despite similar sound.
entries.definitionCN: 和蔼可亲的；源自拉丁语 amare「爱」，词根不同但读音相近，易混。

entries.definition: obeying rules or requests, sometimes with a hint of passivity.
entries.definitionCN: 顺从的、依从的，有时略带被动意味。

entries.definition: easily controlled or managed, like docile animals or solvable problems.
entries.definitionCN: 易驾驭的、易处理的，既可指温驯也可指问题易解。

entries.definition: willing to receive new ideas or suggestions.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于接受新想法或建议的。

normalIntro.en: Link amenable to being led without resistance.
normalIntro.cn: 把 amenable 联想为「不抵抗地被牵引」。

normal.en: a- (to) + men- (drive, lead): one who is led easily.
normal.cn: a-（向）+ men-（驱赶、引导）：容易被牵引的人。

normal.en: Same men- family: amenable, menace (threat used to drive), amenable to reason.
normal.cn: men- 词族：amenable（顺从的）、menace（用于驱赶的威吓）、服理。

normal.en: Picture a farmer leading a calm ox — amenable to the rope.
normal.cn: 想象农夫牵着一头安静的牛——对缰绳十分顺从。

normal.en: Common pattern: amenable to + noun (change, reason, treatment).
normal.cn: 常见搭配：amenable to + 名词（改变、道理、治疗）。

normal.en: Contrast: amendable = can be fixed; amenable = willing to follow.
normal.cn: 对比：amendable 是「可修改」，amenable 是「愿意服从」。

abstract.en: Imagine a door with no lock: it opens amenable to every knock.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没上锁的门：谁来敲都乐意开，即「顺从配合」。

abstract.en: See a meeting where everyone nods; the whole room is amenable.
abstract.cn: 想象会议室里人人点头，全场都「乐于配合」。

abstract.en: Think of soft clay: amenable to every shape the sculptor wants.
abstract.cn: 想想柔软的陶泥：任凭雕塑家摆弄，即「易处理、顺从」。

examples.en: She is amenable to working weekends if the deadline requires it.
examples.cn: 如果截止日期需要，她愿意周末加班。

examples.en: The dispute was finally resolved because both sides were amenable to mediation.
examples.cn: 双方都愿意接受调解，争端最终得到解决。

examples.en: Early-stage illness is far more amenable to treatment.
examples.cn: 早期疾病对治疗的反应要好得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿妹闹不」——阿妹一点也不闹，别人说什么都是「不闹、都行」，特别顺从好说话。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 minare（驱赶牲畜）→ 中世纪拉丁语 aminabilis（可被牵引的）→ 盎格鲁-法语 amener（带来），进入英语后由「应被追究」转为「愿意被引导」，词根属「牵引」意象，词源链条中段存在重构成分。

sensesIntro.en: From the image of a tractable animal being led, amenable extends to legal obedience, workable data, and treatable illness.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「温驯牲畜被牵引」的意象出发，amenable 扩展到法律服从、数据可分析、疾病可治疗等用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calm animal that lets itself be led
core.cn: 核心意象：甘愿被牵引的温驯牲畜

branches.en: Agreeable temperament, in people and animals
branches.cn: 人与动物温顺配合的性情

branches.en: Falling under legal or institutional authority
branches.cn: 受法律或机构权威管辖

branches.en: Problems and data that yield to analysis
branches.cn: 可被分析方法处理的问题与数据

branches.en: Diseases that respond to therapy
branches.cn: 对治疗有反应的疾病

branches.en: Things bound by rules and conditions
branches.cn: 受规则条件约束的事物

intro.en: Amenable combines a prefix of direction, a root of driving, and an adjective suffix of capability.
intro.cn: amensible 由方向前缀、「驱赶」词根和表示能力的形容词后缀组合而成。

latinIntro.en: The root family spreads through words of threat and leading.
latinIntro.cn: 该词族散布于表示威吓与引导的词汇中。

items.example: amener means to bring toward
items.exampleCN: 法语 amener 意为「带来」

items.example: readable means able to be read
items.exampleCN: readable 意为「可读的」

items.example: drunk drivers are a menace
items.exampleCN: 酒后驾车的司机是威胁

items.example: a minatory letter from the bank
items.exampleCN: 银行寄来的威吓信函

items.meaningCN: 和蔼可亲的；注意词根是 amare「爱」
items.example: an amiable host greeted us
items.exampleCN: 和蔼的主人迎接了我们

items.example: they reached an amicable settlement
items.exampleCN: 他们达成了友好和解

items.example: compliant staff followed the rules
items.exampleCN: 守规矩的员工遵守规则

items.example: a tractable problem in math
items.exampleCN: 数学中易解的问题

items.example: a manageable workload
items.exampleCN: 可承受的工作量

items.example: the contract is amendable by both parties
items.exampleCN: 合同双方均可修订

definition_zh: 教育；培养；教育学；（尤指）学校教育体系
definition_en: the process of teaching and learning, especially in schools, and the organized system that carries it out
core_image: 午后教室里的黑板、成排课桌与摊开的课本，窗台上摆着一只装满粉笔的旧铁盒
scene: 乡村学校的教室里，黑板擦得发亮，课桌排成几行，课本摊在桌面上。 Public education gave every child in the valley a seat and a teacher.
sceneCN: 这里指「教与学的过程，尤指学校中的教育」（第 1 个义项：传授与习得知识的过程）；句意为公共教育让山谷里的每个孩子都有了座位和老师。可辨识物件：黑板、课桌、课本、粉笔盒。

pos.zh: 教育；培养；教育学（通常不可数；指一种教育经历时可加不定冠词）

forms.label: 形容词（教育的；教育性的）

senses.title: The process of teaching and learning
senses.definition: the activity through which knowledge, skills and habits are passed from one person to another
senses.definitionCN: 知识、技能与习惯在人与人之间传递的活动
senses.example: Good education begins with questions rather than answers.
senses.exampleCN: 好的教育从提问而不是从答案开始。
senses.why: the noun came from a verb meaning to bring up and rear, so its core is the whole act of raising someone's mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词出自表「养育、培养」的动词，其核心是把人的心智养成的整个动作。

senses.title: The school system
senses.definition: the organized network of schools, teachers, curricula and funding that a state or community maintains
senses.definitionCN: 国家或社区维持的学校、教师、课程与经费的组织网络
senses.example: Rural education improved after the new schools opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新学校开办之后，乡村教育得到改善。
senses.why: once schooling became a public service, the word shifted from the act to the machine that delivers it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦学校教育成为公共服务，这个词就从动作转向提供它的那台机器。

senses.title: A person's upbringing and formation
senses.titleCN: 一个人的教养与成长背景
senses.definition: the whole formation of a person's character and taste, including what happens outside school
senses.definitionCN: 一个人性格与品味所受的整体养成，包括校门之外的部分
senses.example: Her education at home was stricter than anything the school imposed.
senses.exampleCN: 她在家所受的教养比学校的一切要求都更严格。
senses.why: the older sense of rearing survives in phrases about a person's background rather than a system.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的「养育」义保留在谈论个人背景的短语里，而不指体系。

senses.title: The academic field of study
senses.definition: the discipline that studies how people learn and how teaching should be organized
senses.definitionCN: 研究人如何学习、教学应如何组织的学科
senses.example: She holds a doctorate in education from a state university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一所州立大学取得教育学博士学位。
senses.why: a field of study takes the name of its object, which is why the discipline is simply called education.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科常以其研究对象命名，因此这门学科直接就叫「教育」。

senses.title: A level or stage of schooling
senses.titleCN: 某一阶段或层级的教育
senses.definition: a named stage such as primary, secondary or higher education
senses.definitionCN: 初等、中等或高等教育等具名阶段
senses.example: Fewer girls than boys continued into secondary education.
senses.exampleCN: 继续升入中等教育的女孩少于男孩。
senses.why: the single word covers each named stage, because a stage is only a portion of the whole process.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词覆盖每一个具名阶段，因为一个阶段只是整个过程中的一段。

senses.title: A public information campaign
senses.titleCN: 面向公众的宣传教育活动
senses.definition: an organized effort to teach the public about health, safety or civic matters
senses.definitionCN: 就健康、安全或公共事务向公众进行的有组织教育
senses.example: The clinic ran a road safety education week.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所办了一周的道路安全教育。
senses.why: the same word covers teaching that has no classroom, because the aim is still to change behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也覆盖没有教室的教学，因为目的仍是改变行为。

senses.title: The teaching profession and its work
senses.definition: the occupation of teachers and the professional work they do
senses.definitionCN: 教师的职业及其专业工作
senses.example: She entered education after ten years in engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 她在工程界工作十年后进入教育行业。
senses.why: the activity became an industry with careers, so the word also names the trade itself.
senses.whyCN: 这项活动成为一个有职业路径的行业，因此这个词也指行业本身。

senses.title: The result: a cultivated mind
senses.titleCN: 教育的结果：被培养出的心智
senses.definition: the knowledge and judgement a person finally possesses as a result of learning
senses.definitionCN: 一个人因学习而最终拥有的知识与判断力
senses.example: His education showed in the way he listened before speaking.
senses.exampleCN: 他的教养体现在他先听后说的方式上。
senses.why: the word can name either the journey or what the traveller carries at the end.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可指旅程，也可指旅人最终带着的东西。

intro.en: Education comes from Latin educatio 'a rearing, training', from educare 'to bring up, rear'. It reached English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 educatio「养育、培养」，其动词为 educare「抚养、培育」，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Educare meant 'to bring up, rear, nurture'. It is generally connected with the idea of drawing out a person's capacities, though the exact pre-Latin shape is not established.
items.cn: educare 意为「抚养、培育、养育」，一般认为与「把人身上的能力引发出来」这一观念相关，但其拉丁语之前的确切形态未获证明。

items.en: Educere, ex- 'out' plus ducere 'to lead', meant 'to lead out'. The famous notion of education as leading a mind out rests on this second verb.
items.cn: educere 由 ex-「向外」加 ducere「引导」构成，意为「引出」。把教育理解为「把心智引出来」的著名说法，依据的正是这第二个动词。

items.en: Educatio named the rearing and training of a child. English took the noun through French with the same meaning.
items.cn: educatio 指对儿童的抚养与训练，英语经法语借入时保留了同一含义。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word increasingly meant formal instruction in schools rather than upbringing at home.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词越来越多地指学校里的正式教学，而非家庭中的养育。

items.en: In the twentieth century education also became the name of the academic discipline that studies teaching and learning.
items.cn: 二十世纪，「教育」又成为研究教与学的学科的正式名称。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether the older verb meant 'nourish' or 'lead out' cannot be settled for the earliest layer, and the link sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'to lead' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：最早一层究竟取「养育」还是「引出」，无法定论；有人把它与表「引导」的词根相连，那只是假说。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin verb that are constantly confused; group two holds near neighbours that name learning.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁动词衍生、极易混淆的词形；第二组是表示学习的近义词。

entries.definition: To teach or bring up someone; the noun education names the whole activity or system, not a single act.
entries.definitionCN: 指教育或培养某人；名词则指整个活动或体系，而非单个动作。

entries.definition: Meaning 'relating to education' or 'instructive', as in an educational visit.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「与教育有关的」或「有教育意义的」，如一次有教育意义的参观。

entries.definition: Describes a person who has received education; it is a state, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 描述受过教育的人，是一种状态，而非体系。

entries.definition: A teacher or someone who works in education; the ending marks the doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指教师或教育工作者，词尾标记施动者。

entries.definition: The formal instruction actually received in schools; it is the measurable part of education.
entries.definitionCN: 指在学校实际受到的正式教学，是教育中可测量的部分。

entries.definition: Practice aimed at a particular skill; it is narrower and usually has a task in view.
entries.definitionCN: 指针对某项技能的练习，范围更窄，通常有具体任务。

entries.definition: The knowledge or skill acquired; it names the result rather than the organized giving.
entries.definitionCN: 指获得的知识或技能，说的是结果而非有组织的传授。

entries.definition: Deliberate teaching of content, often in steps; it is a method within education.
entries.definitionCN: 指有步骤地教授内容，是教育之内的种方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The family runs educate, educated, educational, educator, educative.
normal.cn: 同族包括「教育」「受过教育的」「教育的」「教育者」「有教育作用的」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stages: primary, secondary and higher education.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：初等、中等与高等教育。

normal.en: One verb has two readings, nourish and lead out, and both survive in how people talk about teaching.
normal.cn: 同一个动词有「养育」与「引出」两种读法，两种都留在人们谈论教学的方式里。

normal.en: The same noun serves the activity, the system and the discipline.
normal.cn: 同一个名词兼指活动、体系与学科。

normal.en: A classroom with a board, desks and books is the easiest picture to hold.
normal.cn: 有黑板、课桌与书本的教室是最容易抓住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp being lit rather than a bucket being filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯被点亮，而不是一只桶被灌满。

abstract.en: Picture a seed given soil, water and time, then growing on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子得到土、水与时间，然后自行生长。

abstract.en: Picture a path with several gates, each opened by a different stage of study.
abstract.cn: 想象一条有几道门的路径，每道门由不同的学习阶段打开。

examples.en: Education is the surest route out of poverty for a whole village.
examples.cn: 对一个村庄来说，教育是摆脱贫困最可靠的路。

examples.en: The ministry spends a third of its budget on basic education.
examples.cn: 该部把三分之一的预算投入基础教育。

examples.en: Her education taught her to read a contract before signing it.
examples.cn: 她所受的教育让她在签字前先读懂合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱丢开心」——把不懂的东西一点点丢掉，心就开了，这就是教育。

root: 拉丁 educare「抚养、培育」构成 educatio「养育、训练」；一般认为它与表「引出」的 educere 相关，但「引出说」属后世解释，最早一层含义不能定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a person is brought up, and that bringing-up is then organized into schools, stages, a profession and a discipline, until it finally names what the person carries away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：一个人被养成人，这种养成随后被组织成学校、阶段、职业与学科，最后用来指那个人带走的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp lit in a room rather than a bucket filled from outside.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋里被点亮的一盏灯，而不是从外面灌满的一只桶。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS FRUIT: teaching is both the journey and the judgement carried home.
branches.cn: 动作与果实：教学既是旅程，也是带回家的判断力。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND THE TRADE: a system of schools needs a profession to run it.
branches.cn: 机器与行业：学校体系需要一支职业队伍来运转。

branches.en: BEFORE AND BEYOND SCHOOL: character is formed at home as much as in class.
branches.cn: 校门内外：性格在家里形成，不比在课堂上少。

branches.en: ORGANIZED KNOWLEDGE: a discipline studies education, while stages divide it.
branches.cn: 被组织起来的知识：一门学科研究教育，而阶段把教育分段。

branches.en: WITHOUT A CLASSROOM: campaigns teach the public where no desk exists.
branches.cn: 没有教室：宣传活动在无课桌处教育公众。

intro.en: The word is a Latin action noun whose verb also builds a compact English family, so it can be read from the verb outward.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁动作名词，其动词在英语里也构成一个紧凑词族，因此可从动词向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin educare 'to rear' and educere 'to lead out' share the element ducere 'to lead'; educatio is the action noun built on the first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 educare「养育」与 educere「引出」共享表「引导」的成分；educatio 是在前一个动词上构成的动作名词。

items.example: The prefix turns leading into a movement out of something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「引导」变成「从某处向外」的动作。

items.example: The root supplies the image of a guide walking ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带来「引路者走在前面」的画面。

items.example: The verb names the whole work of raising a child.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指抚养孩子的全部工作。

items.example: They educate their children at home until six.
items.exampleCN: 孩子在六岁前由他们在家教育。

items.meaning: the act, system or result of teaching
items.example: Education changes what a family can imagine.
items.exampleCN: 教育改变一个家庭所能想象的东西。

items.example: The museum runs educational programs for schools.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆为学校开设教育项目。

items.example: The educator trained new teachers in the district.
items.exampleCN: 这位教育工作者在本区培训新教师。

items.example: Failure can be educative if it is examined.
items.exampleCN: 失败若被审视，也能起教育作用。

definition_zh: 异常的；反常的；不合规则的；不合同类模式的
definition_en: deviating from a general rule or from the pattern shared by other members of a class
core_image: 同一批模具压出的零件中，有一个尺寸不合规，无法与其余零件装配齐平
scene: 同一批零件里有一个尺寸不合规，质检员把它单独挑出来。 One part in the batch has an anomalous size, so the inspector picks it out and puts it in a separate box.
sceneCN: 这里 anomalous 是「不合同类模式的」（第 2 个义项：与同类其他成员共享的模式不一致）；句意：同一批零件里有一个尺寸异常，质检员把它挑出来放进单独的盒子。场景要点：流水线上的同批零件、卡尺、标红的尺寸、单独的收纳盒、质检员的手。

pos.zh: 异常的；反常的；不合规则的

collocations.zh: 异常位置；不合常理的位置

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Not conforming to a general rule
senses.definition: deviating from what is usual or from a general rule
senses.definitionCN: 偏离通常情况或一般规则的
senses.example: The committee received an anomalous report of a bird nesting in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会收到一份反常的报告，说有一种鸟在冬天筑巢。
senses.why: The adjective describes the member that fails the rule; -ous means 'having the nature of', so anomalous = having the nature of a deviation.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述那个不服从规则的成员；-ous 意为“具有……的性质”，所以 anomalous 就是“具有偏离性质的”。

senses.title: Not fitting the pattern of its class
senses.definition: not matching the pattern shared by other members of the same class or type
senses.definitionCN: 与同类其他成员共享的模式不一致
senses.example: An anomalous mineral in the sample did not match the surrounding rock.
senses.exampleCN: 样本里有一种异常矿物，与周围岩石并不匹配。
senses.why: The Greek image is 'not even with its neighbours'. The word stresses mismatch within a class, not mere rarity.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语意象是“与邻居不齐平”。这个词强调类别内部的不匹配，而不是单纯的罕见。

senses.title: Inconsistent with a scientific model
senses.definition: inconsistent with an established scientific model or expected result
senses.definitionCN: 与既有科学模型或预期结果不一致的
senses.example: The probe sent back anomalous readings before it failed.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器在失灵前发回了异常读数。
senses.why: When a measurement does not fit the model, the adjective marks the reading as suspect; the noun anomaly names the reading itself.
senses.whyCN: 当测量不符合模型时，形容词把读数标记为可疑；名词 anomaly 则命名读数本身。

senses.title: Departing from normal anatomy
senses.definition: describing a structure or development that departs from the usual anatomical pattern
senses.definitionCN: 描述偏离通常解剖模式的结构或发育
senses.example: The scan showed an anomalous blood vessel near the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示心脏附近有一根异常血管。
senses.why: Medicine uses the class-pattern sense for anatomy: the vessel is anomalous because it does not follow the usual branching pattern.
senses.whyCN: 医学把“类别模式”义用于解剖：这根血管之所以是 anomalous，是因为它不按通常的分支模式生长。

senses.title: Outside the expected distribution
senses.definition: lying outside the expected distribution or pattern in a data set
senses.definitionCN: 在数据集中落在预期分布或模式之外的
senses.example: An anomalous cluster of cases appeared in the northern district.
senses.exampleCN: 北部地区出现了一组异常病例。
senses.why: Statistics makes 'expected' numerical; a point far from the distribution is anomalous, and the adjective often precedes 'result' or 'data'.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把“预期”变成数值；远离分布的点就是 anomalous，这个形容词常放在 result 或 data 之前。

senses.title: Unusual against social norms
senses.titleCN: 违反社会规范而显得反常的
senses.definition: unusual in a way that does not fit the norms of a group or situation
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常到不符合某个群体或情境规范的程度
senses.example: His anomalous silence during the meeting worried his colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上反常的沉默让同事们担心。
senses.why: Social norms are rules too; behavior that does not match them is described as anomalous, often suggesting something is wrong or unexplained.
senses.whyCN: 社会规范也是规则；不符合规范的行为会被描述为 anomalous，通常暗示出了什么问题或有什么无法解释。

senses.title: Contradicting a market model
senses.definition: producing a return or pattern that contradicts an accepted market model
senses.definitionCN: 产生与公认市场模型相矛盾的收益或模式
senses.example: The fund was built to profit from anomalous pricing between two markets.
senses.exampleCN: 这只基金旨在从两个市场之间的异常定价中获利。
senses.why: Finance treats market models as rules; a persistent exception is anomalous, whether it is a price gap or a seasonal effect.
senses.whyCN: 金融把市场模型当作规则；持续存在的例外就是 anomalous，无论它表现为价格差还是季节性效应。

senses.title: Irregular in linguistic form
senses.definition: not following the regular inflection or sound pattern of a language
senses.definitionCN: 不遵循某种语言的规则屈折或语音模式
senses.example: The anomalous plural was memorized as a single exception.
senses.exampleCN: 那个不规则复数被当作单个例外记住了。
senses.why: A language's regular forms are generated by rules; an irregular form is anomalous because it does not share the class pattern, though native speakers use it easily.
senses.whyCN: 语言的规则形式由规则生成；不规则形式之所以是 anomalous，是因为它不共享类别模式，尽管母语者用起来毫不费力。

senses.title: Inconsistent with a logical system
senses.definition: not consistent with an accepted principle or with the rest of a system
senses.definitionCN: 与公认原则或体系其余部分不一致的
senses.example: The hypothesis was rejected because it left an anomalous set of facts unexplained.
senses.exampleCN: 这个假说被否定了，因为它留下一组无法解释的反常事实。
senses.why: In logic and philosophy, a fact that will not fit the system is anomalous; the word names the friction between a case and its governing rule.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑和哲学中，无法嵌入体系的事实就是 anomalous；这个词命名个案与其统辖规则之间的摩擦。

intro.en: Anomalous is the adjective from the same Greek stem as anomaly: Greek anomalos 'uneven, irregular' (an- 'not' + homalos 'even', from homos 'same'). It reached English in the 1640s through Late Latin anomalus, with the English adjective ending -ous. The core is 'deviating from the rule of its class', not 'rare'. Normal comes from Latin norma and is unrelated; abnormal is a reshaped borrowing of the same Greek word, altered under norma's influence.
intro.cn: anomalous 是与 anomaly 同出希腊词干的形容词：希腊语 anomalos“不平整、不规则”（an-“不”+ homalos“平的”，后者来自 homos“同一”）。它于 17 世纪 40 年代经晚期拉丁语 anomalus 进入英语，并带英语形容词词尾 -ous。核心是“偏离同类规则”，而不是“罕见”。normal 来自拉丁语 norma，与之无关；abnormal 是同一希腊词在 norma 影响下被改写的借词。

items.en: First recorded as 'deviating from a general rule', borrowed through Late Latin anomalus from Greek anomalos.
items.cn: 最早记录为“偏离一般规则的”，经晚期拉丁语 anomalus 借自希腊语 anomalos。

items.en: anomalus is the Latinized form of Greek anomalos 'uneven, irregular'; it keeps the Greek negative an-, not Latin in- or ab-.
items.cn: anomalus 是希腊语 anomalos“不平整、不规则”的拉丁化形式；它保留希腊语否定前缀 an-，而不是拉丁语 in- 或 ab-。

items.en: anomalos = an- 'not' + homalos 'even, level'. homalos is built on homos 'same', from PIE *sem- 'one, together'.
items.cn: anomalos = an-“不”+ homalos“平的、水平的”。homalos 由 homos“同一”构成，后者来自原始印欧语 *sem-“一、共同”。

items.en: The adjective ending -ous comes from Old French -ous and Latin -osus; added to anomalus it gives 'having the nature of the uneven or irregular'. The noun anomaly was already in English.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -ous 来自古法语 -ous 和拉丁语 -osus；加在 anomalus 上得到“具有不平整或不规则性质的”。名词 anomaly 当时已进入英语。

items.en: The core is not 'rare' but 'not conforming to the same measure as the class'. A member that fails the pattern is anomalous; the pattern itself may be perfectly ordinary.
items.cn: 核心不是“罕见”，而是“不与同类共用同一尺度”。不满足模式的成员是 anomalous；模式本身可能完全普通。

items.en: Anomalous result, data and behavior are the common collocations. Normal is unrelated (norma); abnormal was reshaped by norma. Anomalous kept the Greek shape and the meaning 'deviating from the rule of its class'.
items.cn: anomalous result、data、behavior 是常见搭配。normal 与之无关（norma）；abnormal 受 norma 影响而被改写。anomalous 保留了希腊语外形和“偏离同类规则”的含义。

note.en: The first group separates the noun and adverb from the adjective and marks normal as a false base; the second compares near synonyms by what kind of 'not normal' they mean.
note.cn: 第一组把名词、副词同形容词分开，并指出 normal 是假词基；第二组按“不正常”的具体类型区分近义词。

entries.definition: a deviation or the thing that deviates. It is the noun; anomalous is the adjective that describes such a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离，或偏离的事物。它是名词；anomalous 是描述这类事物的形容词。

entries.definition: in a deviating manner. It modifies an action, while anomalous modifies a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以偏离的方式。它修饰动作，而 anomalous 修饰名词。

entries.definition: usual or conforming to a standard, from norma 'carpenter's square'. It is not the positive base of anomalous.
entries.definitionCN: 通常的或符合标准的，来自 norma“木匠曲尺”。它不是 anomalous 的肯定词基。

entries.definition: deviating from the normal and often suggesting harm. It is historically a reshaped borrowing of Greek anomalos, not a clean negative of normal.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离正常的，常暗示有害。它在历史上是对希腊语 anomalos 的改写借词，不是 normal 的干净否定形式。

entries.definition: not representative of its type. It stresses rarity or unrepresentativeness, while anomalous stresses failure to conform to a rule or class pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 不能代表其类型的。它强调罕见或不具代表性，而 anomalous 强调不符合规则或类别模式。

entries.definition: departing from an accepted standard, often in behavior or biology. It carries a stronger sense of going astray than anomalous.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离公认标准的，常用于行为或生物学。它比 anomalous 带有更强的“走入歧途”意味。

entries.definition: not regular in form, spacing, or occurrence. It can describe a pattern; anomalous usually describes a case that contradicts the pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 在形状、间隔或发生上不规则的。它可以描述一个模式；anomalous 通常描述违背该模式的个案。

entries.definition: unusually good or unusually different. It often carries approval, whereas anomalous is neutral or suspicious.
entries.definitionCN: 异常地好或异常地不同。它常带有赞许意味，而 anomalous 是中性的或带怀疑的。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek anomalos, the adjective ending -ous, the noun anomaly, and the false resemblance to normal from norma.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 anomalos、形容词词尾 -ous、名词 anomaly，以及与 norma 来的 normal 之间的假相似。

normal.en: Greek anomalos 'not even' + Latin -ous 'having the nature of': anomalous means 'having the nature of a deviation'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 anomalos“不平的”+ 拉丁 -ous“具有……性质的”：anomalous 意为“具有偏离性质的”。

normal.en: anomaly is the noun, anomalous the adjective, anomalously the adverb; the endings do the grammar, not the meaning.
normal.cn: anomaly 是名词，anomalous 是形容词，anomalously 是副词；词尾负责语法，不改变核心含义。

normal.en: Do not read a + normal: normal is from norma 'carpenter's square', a different root.
normal.cn: 不要读成 a + normal：normal 来自 norma“木匠曲尺”，是不同词根。

normal.en: abnormal began as anormal, a borrowing of Greek anomalos altered under the influence of norma; its history is tangled, so treat it as a near synonym, not a clean negative.
normal.cn: abnormal 最初是 anormal，是希腊语 anomalos 在 norma 影响下被改写的借词；它的历史是纠缠的，所以应把它当作近义词，而不是干净的否定形式。

normal.en: Common collocations: anomalous result, anomalous data, anomalous behavior; each points to a case that fails the class pattern.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：anomalous result、anomalous data、anomalous behavior；每一个都指向不符合类别模式的个案。

abstract.en: A set of identical keys cut from one pattern: one key will not turn the lock because its teeth are not even with the others. It is anomalous.
abstract.cn: 一组按同一模板切出的钥匙：有一把插不进锁，因为它的齿与其余不齐。它就是 anomalous。

abstract.en: A flock of birds all flying in one direction: one bird keeps a different angle; the adjective describes that bird, not the flock.
abstract.cn: 一群鸟都朝一个方向飞：有一只保持不同角度；这个形容词描述的是那只鸟，而不是整群。

abstract.en: A printed page with one letter in a different font: the letter is anomalous because it does not share the rule of the page, even though it is readable.
abstract.cn: 一页印刷文字里有一个字母用了不同字体：这个字母是 anomalous，因为它不共享整页的规则，尽管它完全可读。

examples.en: The experiment produced an anomalous result that the team repeated three times.
examples.cn: 实验产生了一个异常结果，团队重复了三次。

examples.en: Water's anomalous expansion makes ice float.
examples.cn: 水的反常膨胀使冰浮在水面上。

examples.en: His anomalous silence made the others uneasy.
examples.cn: 他反常的沉默让其他人不安。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安 no 马勒斯」——‘俺 no 麻利’还偏要乱来 → anomalous 异常的、不合规的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 希腊语 anomalos“不平整、不规则”（an- 不 + homalos 平的）+ 拉丁形容词词尾 -ous；核心是“偏离同类规则”，与 normal（norma）无关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of anomalous all describe a case that fails a pattern: a general rule, its class, a scientific model, anatomy, a distribution, social norms, a market model, a language's inflection, or a logical system.
sensesIntro.cn: anomalous 的九个义项都描述一个不满足模式的个案：一般规则、所属类别、科学模型、解剖结构、数据分布、社会规范、市场模型、语言屈折或逻辑体系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a member that is not level with the pattern shared by its class.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个与同类共享模式不齐平的成员。

branches.en: THE CORE: failing a general rule and failing the specific pattern of one's class.
branches.cn: 核心：不服从一般规则，也不符合所属类别的具体模式。

branches.en: MODELS AND DATA: a reading or cluster that the model or distribution cannot accommodate.
branches.cn: 模型与数据：模型或分布无法容纳的读数或集群。

branches.en: ANATOMY: a structure that departs from the usual developmental pattern.
branches.cn: 解剖：偏离通常发育模式的结构。

branches.en: NORMS AND LOGIC: behavior or a fact that will not fit the group's norms or the system's principles.
branches.cn: 规范与逻辑：无法嵌入群体规范或体系原则的行为或事实。

branches.en: SPECIALIZED RULES: market models and linguistic inflection patterns each define what counts as anomalous.
branches.cn: 专门规则：市场模型与语言屈折模式各自界定什么算 anomalous。

intro.en: Anomalous is Late Latin anomalus (from Greek anomalos) + the English adjective ending -ous. The Greek compound is an- 'not' + homalos 'even' (from homos 'same'); -ous adds 'having the nature of'. The noun anomaly is the same stem with -y. Normal belongs to Latin norma and is not the base.
intro.cn: anomalous 是晚期拉丁语 anomalus（来自希腊语 anomalos）+ 英语形容词词尾 -ous。希腊语复合词是 an-“不”+ homalos“平的”（来自 homos“同一”）；-ous 加上“具有……性质”。名词 anomaly 是同一词干加 -y。normal 属于拉丁语 norma，并不是它的词基。

latinIntro.en: Latin anomalus is only a Latinized Greek adjective; the compound's parts are Greek. Latin supplies the adjective ending -ous. The separate Latin family norma -> normalis -> normal is the source of the word that anomaly is mistakenly thought to negate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 anomalus 只是希腊语形容词的拉丁化形式；复合词的各部分是希腊语的。拉丁语提供形容词词尾 -ous。另一支拉丁词族 norma -> normalis -> normal，才是人们误以为 anomaly 所要否定的那个词的来源。

items.meaning: having the nature of a deviation from rule
items.meaningCN: 具有偏离规则性质的；异常的（-ous 构成形容词）
items.example: The anomalous signal disappeared after the antenna was moved.
items.exampleCN: 天线移动后，那个异常信号消失了。

items.structure: Greek anomalia (abstract noun), borrowed through Latin
items.meaning: a deviation; the thing that deviates
items.meaningCN: 偏离；偏离的事物（希腊语抽象名词）
items.example: The anomaly was logged and sent to the team.
items.exampleCN: 这个异常被记录并发送给了团队。

items.meaningCN: 不平整的；不规则的（an- 不 + homalos 平的）
items.example: anomalos is the Greek source of both anomalous and anomaly.
items.exampleCN: anomalos 是 anomalous 与 anomaly 的共同希腊语来源。

items.example: The an- here is Greek, not the Latin in-.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 an- 是希腊语前缀，不是拉丁语 in-。

items.meaningCN: 平的；水平的（来自 homos“同一”）
items.example: A homalos surface is level with its neighbours.
items.exampleCN: homalos 的表面与邻近部分齐平。

items.example: homos underlies several Greek words about sameness.
items.exampleCN: homos 是若干表示“相同”的希腊词的词根。

items.meaningCN: 异常地；不合规则地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The metal expanded anomalously when cooled.
items.exampleCN: 这种金属冷却时反常地膨胀。

items.meaningCN: 异常性；不合规则的性质（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The anomalousness of the pattern attracted notice.
items.exampleCN: 这个模式的异常性引起了注意。

items.structure: anormal (altered from Greek anomalos) reshaped under Latin norma
items.meaning: deviating from the normal, often suggesting harm
items.meaningCN: 异常的；反常的（常含不良意味；拼写受 norma 影响）
items.example: The abnormal result was checked against the reference range.
items.exampleCN: 那个异常结果被对照参考范围核查。

items.meaningCN: 正常的；符合标准的（来自 norma 曲尺、规则）
items.example: The normal reading falls inside the printed range.
items.exampleCN: 正常读数落在印出的范围之内。

latinEntries.structure: Late Latin borrowing of Greek anomalos
Latin noun of uncertain origin; 'carpenter's square, rule'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 规则；模式；标准（与 anomalous 无关的对照词）

definition_zh: 食肉的；肉食性的
definition_en: describing an animal or plant that feeds on animal flesh, or a diet based on meat
core_image: 一枚刀状裂齿咬合另一枚，像剪刀一样把韧带剪断
scene: 这里指「食肉的」。 Carnivorous plants such as sundews digest insects to supplement the poor soil.
sceneCN: 这里 carnivorous 指「食肉的」（第 1 个义项：以动物肉体为食）；茅膏菜等食肉植物消化昆虫，以弥补贫瘠土壤的养分。图中可辨识物件：裂齿、剪刀状咬合、茅膏菜、昆虫。

pos.zh: 食肉的；肉食性的（比较级 more carnivorous，最高级 most carnivorous）

derivatives.zh: 裂齿的；食肉动物的剪切齿

senses.title: Flesh as the main food
senses.titleCN: 食肉性：以动物肉体为主要食物
senses.definition: describing an animal whose diet is mainly the flesh of other animals
senses.definitionCN: 描述以其他动物的肉体为主要食物的动物
senses.example: The carnivorous beetle hunts smaller insects in the leaf litter.
senses.exampleCN: 这种肉食性甲虫在落叶层中猎食更小的昆虫。
senses.why: The adjective states a diet class, so it can describe any animal without committing to a taxonomic group.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词陈述食性类别，因此能描述任何动物，而不必归属于某个分类群。

senses.title: Carnivorous plants
senses.definition: describing a plant that traps and digests small animals to obtain nitrogen or other nutrients
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过捕获并消化小动物来获取氮等养分的植物
senses.example: The bog is full of carnivorous plants that thrive where roots cannot feed.
senses.exampleCN: 这片酸性泥炭沼泽满是食虫植物，它们在根系无法取食的地方繁茂生长。
senses.why: The plant does not hunt for energy but for minerals, so the adjective is borrowed for a nutrient strategy.
senses.whyCN: 这些植物捕猎不是为了能量，而是为了矿物质，因此这个形容词被借来描述一种养分策略。

senses.title: Carnivorous dinosaurs
senses.titleCN: 肉食恐龙：以化石齿型判定
senses.definition: describing extinct reptiles identified as meat eaters from curved, serrated teeth and jaw mechanics
senses.definitionCN: 描述依据弯曲锯齿状牙齿与颌部力学判定为食肉的已灭绝爬行动物
senses.example: Carnivorous dinosaurs such as tyrannosaurs had recurved serrated teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 暴龙这类肉食恐龙长有向后弯的锯齿状牙齿。
senses.why: Palaeontology reads diet from morphology, so the adjective often appears beside tooth and jaw evidence.
senses.whyCN: 古生物学从形态读出食性，因此这个形容词常与牙齿和颌部证据一起出现。

senses.title: Carnivorous fish
senses.titleCN: 肉食鱼类：以其他鱼或甲壳类为食
senses.definition: describing fish that prey on other fish, crustaceans or molluscs
senses.definitionCN: 描述捕食其他鱼、甲壳类或软体动物的鱼类
senses.example: Carnivorous fish dominate the upper levels of the reef food web.
senses.exampleCN: 肉食鱼类主导礁体食物网的上层。
senses.why: Aquaculture and fisheries use the label to separate feed requirements, since carnivorous fish need protein-rich feed.
senses.whyCN: 水产养殖与渔业用这个标签区分饲料需求，因为肉食鱼需要高蛋白饲料。

senses.title: Carnivorous mammals
senses.titleCN: 肉食哺乳动物：裂齿与咬合
senses.definition: describing mammals with shearing carnassial teeth and jaws built for cutting flesh
senses.definitionCN: 描述具有剪切裂齿与适合切割肉类的颌部的哺乳动物
senses.example: The carnivorous skull has a short jaw and powerful bite muscles.
senses.exampleCN: 肉食性头骨具有短颌与强劲咬肌。
senses.why: Mammalian carnivory has a distinctive anatomical signature, and the adjective often flags that signature in fossils.
senses.whyCN: 哺乳动物食肉有独特的解剖签名，这个形容词常在化石中标出该签名。

senses.title: Carnivorous birds
senses.titleCN: 肉食鸟类：猛禽与食肉水鸟
senses.definition: describing birds that hunt or scavenge animal flesh, such as hawks, owls and vultures
senses.definitionCN: 描述猎食或食腐动物肉的鸟类，如鹰、鸮与秃鹫
senses.example: Carnivorous birds concentrate at the river during the fish run.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼汛期间，肉食鸟类聚集在河边。
senses.why: Flight adds a hunting style of its own, but the diet label stays the same as for ground predators.
senses.whyCN: 飞行带来独特的狩猎方式，但食性标签与地面捕食者相同。

senses.title: A carnivorous human diet
senses.titleCN: 人类肉食饮食：以肉为主的食谱
senses.definition: describing a human diet that is based mainly or entirely on animal products
senses.definitionCN: 描述主要或完全以动物性食物为基础的人类饮食
senses.example: The clinic studied a carnivorous diet low in fibre and high in fat.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所研究了一种低纤维、高脂肪的肉食饮食。
senses.why: Here the adjective moves from zoology to nutrition, where it labels a diet rather than a species.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个形容词从动物学移到营养学，标注的是食谱而非物种。

senses.title: Carnivorous behaviour in insects
senses.titleCN: 昆虫的肉食行为：捕食与寄生
senses.definition: describing insects that kill and eat other insects, whether as hunters or as parasitoids
senses.definitionCN: 描述杀死并取食其他昆虫的昆虫，无论是捕食者还是拟寄生者
senses.example: Carnivorous wasps are used to control caterpillar pests.
senses.exampleCN: 肉食性蜂类被用来控制毛虫害虫。
senses.why: Biological control depends on this label, because only a flesh-eating insect can regulate a pest population.
senses.whyCN: 生物防治依赖这个标签，因为只有食肉的昆虫才能调节害虫种群。

intro.en: Carnivorous is the Latin adjective carnivorus, from caro 'flesh' and vorare 'devour'. It is the adjectival twin of the noun carnivore.
intro.cn: carnivorous 是拉丁形容词 carnivorus，由 caro「肉」与 vorare「吞食」构成，是名词 carnivore 的形容词孪生形式。

items.en: Caro, carnis meant flesh or meat, and it also survives in carnal and carnage.
items.cn: caro, carnis 意为肉或肉体，也保存在 carnal 与 carnage 中。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour. The compound pattern -vorus 'eating' was used for diet adjectives in scientific Latin.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食；复合成分 -vorus「吃……的」在科学拉丁语中用于构成食性形容词。

items.en: Carnivorus was the standard adjective for flesh-eating in modern scientific Latin, and its exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: carnivorus 是近代科学拉丁语中表示食肉的标准形容词，确切首用存疑。

items.en: English carnivorous appears in the seventeenth century, earlier than the noun in common use. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 carnivorous 在 17 世纪出现，比名词的通行用法更早；确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: The plant sense developed in the nineteenth century as botanists described species that trap insects.
items.cn: 植物义在 19 世纪发展出来，当时植物学家描述捕虫的物种。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vorous ending and differs by stem; the near-meaning group separates diet, behaviour and taxonomy.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vorous 结尾而词干不同；近义组区分食性、行为与分类。

entries.definition: The animal or plant itself. Use carnivorous when the word must modify a noun, as in carnivorous plant.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物或植物本身。需要修饰名词时应使用 carnivorous，如 carnivorous plant。

entries.definition: Describes a plant diet. The stem herba- is the only difference, and the two adjectives mark opposite diets.
entries.definitionCN: 描述植食。词干 herba- 是唯一差别，两个形容词标示相反食性。

entries.definition: Describes a mixed diet. It is broader than carnivorous, because plant food is included.
entries.definitionCN: 描述混合食性。它比 carnivorous 更宽，因为包含植物性食物。

entries.definition: Describes hunting and killing. A carnivorous animal may live on carrion and never hunt, so the two adjectives answer different questions.
entries.definitionCN: 描述猎杀行为。食肉动物可能靠腐肉为生而从不狩猎，因此两个形容词回答不同问题。

entries.definition: A transparent compound with the same meaning but no scientific register. It is common in news writing about outbreaks.
entries.definitionCN: 透明的复合词，含义相同但不带科学语域，常见于疫情新闻报道。

entries.definition: Describes a diet of insects. It is a narrower class that can fall inside carnivorous.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以昆虫为食，是更窄的类别，可归入食肉范畴。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: caro 'flesh' + -vorous 'eating': flesh-eating.
normal.cn: caro「肉」+ -vorous「吃……的」：食肉的。

normal.en: Typical phrases: carnivorous plant, carnivorous dinosaur, carnivorous fish, carnivorous diet.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：食虫植物、肉食恐龙、肉食鱼类、肉食饮食。

normal.en: The family runs carnivore, carnivory, carnassial and Carnivora.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 carnivore、carnivory、carnassial、Carnivora。

normal.en: Carnivorous answers what it eats; predatory answers how it gets it.
normal.cn: carnivorous 回答吃什么；predatory 回答怎么得到。

normal.en: The plant sense is about minerals, not energy: the bog soil is too poor for roots.
normal.cn: 植物义关乎矿物质而非能量：沼泽土壤太贫瘠，根系取不到养分。

abstract.en: Picture two blade-like teeth sliding past each other like scissors.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚刀状齿像剪刀一样相互滑过。

abstract.en: Picture a sundew's sticky tentacles curling around a fly.
abstract.cn: 想象茅膏菜的黏性触须卷住一只苍蝇。

abstract.en: Picture a hawk's curved beak tearing a fish on the riverbank.
abstract.cn: 想象鹰的弯喙在河岸撕开一条鱼。

examples.en: Carnivorous plants grow where the soil lacks nitrogen.
examples.cn: 食虫植物生长在缺氮的土壤上。

examples.en: The carnivorous dinosaur's teeth were built for slicing, not grinding.
examples.cn: 这种肉食恐龙的牙齿适合切割而非研磨。

examples.en: Carnivorous fish require high-protein feed in captivity.
examples.cn: 肉食性鱼类在人工饲养下需要高蛋白饲料。

dict_mnemonic.text: carnivore（食肉动物）+ ous（……的）→ 食肉的 → carnivorous

root: 拉丁 caro, carnis「肉」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 carnivorus「食肉的」→ 英语 carnivorous。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply the flesh-diet adjective to animals, plants, fossils, fish, mammals, birds, human diets and insects.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个食肉形容词用于动物、植物、化石、鱼类、哺乳动物、鸟类、人类饮食与昆虫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two blade-like teeth sliding together like scissors.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚刀状齿像剪刀一样咬合。

branches.en: DIET: the base sense says flesh is the main food.
branches.cn: 食性：基本义说肉是主要食物。

branches.en: PLANTS: the adjective is borrowed for a mineral strategy, not a hunt for energy.
branches.cn: 植物：这个形容词被借来描述养分策略，而非为能量捕猎。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: teeth and jaws let the label be read from fossils.
branches.cn: 深层时间：牙齿与颌部让这个标签能从化石读出。

branches.en: HUNTERS: fish, birds and insects show how many forms the flesh diet takes.
branches.cn: 猎手：鱼、鸟与昆虫展示了食肉方式的多样形态。

branches.en: NUTRITION: the same adjective labels a human diet rather than a species.
branches.cn: 营养：同一个形容词标注人类食谱而非物种。

intro.en: Carnivorous is the adjective branch of the -vore family, with caro- 'flesh' as its stem.
intro.cn: carnivorous 是 -vore 词族中的形容词支，词干为 caro-「肉」。

latinIntro.en: Caro is a third-declension noun, vorare a first-conjugation verb, and -vorus the adjective ending used in diet compounds.
latinIntro.cn: caro 是第三变格名词，vorare 是第一变格动词，-vorus 是食性复合词中的形容词词尾。

items.example: The carnivorous snail drills into other shells.
items.exampleCN: 这种肉食性螺钻进其他贝壳。

items.example: The carnivore hunts at night.
items.exampleCN: 这只食肉动物夜间狩猎。

items.example: Carnivory evolved repeatedly in mammals.
items.exampleCN: 食肉习性在哺乳动物中多次演化。

items.example: The carnassials meet like scissors.
items.exampleCN: 裂齿像剪刀一样咬合。

items.example: Carnivora contains seals as well as cats.
items.exampleCN: 食肉目既含海豹也含猫。

items.example: Herbivorous mammals have flat molars.
items.exampleCN: 植食哺乳动物臼齿扁平。

items.example: Omnivorous animals switch with the season.
items.exampleCN: 杂食动物随季节切换食物。

items.example: Insectivorous birds nest in the orchard.
items.exampleCN: 食虫鸟类在果园筑巢。

items.example: The flood left carnage along the valley.
items.exampleCN: 洪水在谷地留下惨烈景象。

latinEntries.structure: vorare, voro, voravi, voratum (v., first conjugation)

definition_zh: 构造板块；岩石圈板块；板块构造学说中的板块单元
definition_en: one of the large rigid pieces of the Earth's lithosphere that slowly move over the weaker mantle beneath
core_image: 球面上拼着许多厚石板，石板边缘相互顶住、错开，底下的软层缓慢流动
scene: 地质课上，教师把几张厚纸板拼成球面，演示坚硬的岩石圈如何裂成若干块并相互推挤。 Each tectonic plate carries both crust and upper mantle and drifts on the softer rock below.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（岩石圈板块）；句意为每个构造板块都包含地壳与上地幔，并在下方较软的岩石上缓慢漂移。

pos.zh: 名词短语：构造板块；岩石圈板块；（板块构造学说中的）板块

derivatives.zh: 由希腊表示「建造」的词加形容词词尾构成，义为「构造的；地壳构造的」
由形容词加学科名词词尾构成，义为「构造地质学；构造作用」
由表示「扁平」的希腊词经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，义为「板；板块；盘子」
由「板块」与「构造学」组合而成，义为「板块构造学说」
由表示「微小」的前缀加「板块」构成，义为「微板块」
由「板块」加表示「边缘」的名词构成，义为「板块边缘」
由「板块」加表示「边界」的名词构成，义为「板块边界」

senses.title: A rigid slab of lithosphere
senses.definition: one of the large rigid pieces of the lithosphere, including crust and uppermost mantle
senses.definitionCN: 指岩石圈中一块巨大而坚硬的板块，包含地壳与上地幔顶部
senses.example: Each tectonic plate carries both crust and upper mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 每个构造板块都包含地壳与上地幔。
senses.why: The Greek builder word supplied the idea of a constructed slab, and the flat-sheet word supplied the shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语中表示「建造者」的词给出「拼装成的厚板」这一想法，表示「扁平」的词给出形状。

senses.title: One of the named major plates
senses.definition: one of the dozen or so large plates that geologists name, such as the Pacific plate
senses.definitionCN: 指地质学家逐一命名的十来块大板块，例如太平洋板块
senses.example: The Pacific tectonic plate is the largest of the named plates.
senses.exampleCN: 太平洋构造板块是具名板块中最大的一个。
senses.why: Once the mosaic was recognized, each piece needed a proper name for maps and papers.
senses.whyCN: 人们认出这幅拼图之后，每一块都需要在图件与论文里有正式名称。

senses.title: An oceanic plate
senses.definition: a plate whose upper part is dense basaltic oceanic crust
senses.definitionCN: 指上部由致密玄武岩质大洋地壳构成的板块
senses.example: An oceanic tectonic plate is thinner and denser than a continental one.
senses.exampleCN: 大洋构造板块比大陆板块更薄、更致密。
senses.why: Ocean floor rock is heavy enough to sink, so plates capped by it behave differently at the edges.
senses.whyCN: 洋底岩石足够重、会下沉，因此以它为顶的板块在边缘处表现不同。

senses.title: A continental plate
senses.definition: a plate whose upper part includes thick, buoyant continental crust
senses.definitionCN: 指上部包含厚实而较轻的大陆地壳的板块
senses.example: The continental tectonic plate rides higher on the mantle.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆构造板块在地幔之上浮得更高。
senses.why: Continental rock is lighter, so the plate floats higher and resists subduction.
senses.whyCN: 大陆岩石更轻，因此板块浮得更高，也不易被俯冲。

senses.title: The edge zone where plates meet
senses.definition: the boundary zone along which two plates converge, diverge or slide past each other
senses.definitionCN: 指两块板块汇聚、分离或相互错动所经过的边界带
senses.example: Most earthquakes cluster along a tectonic plate edge.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数地震集中在构造板块边缘。
senses.why: The slab is rigid only in the middle; its rim is where all the friction and fracture happen.
senses.whyCN: 板块只有中部是刚性的，边缘才是摩擦与破裂集中发生的地方。

senses.title: The slow drift of a plate
senses.definition: the movement of a plate over the weaker mantle, usually measured in centimetres per year
senses.definitionCN: 指板块在较软弱的地幔之上移动，通常以每年若干厘米计
senses.example: The tectonic plate moves a few centimetres each year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个构造板块每年移动几厘米。
senses.why: The word plate suggests something fixed, yet the whole point of the theory is that it travels.
senses.whyCN: 「板」这个词让人想到固定不动，而这套理论的要点恰是它在移动。

senses.title: A small independent plate
senses.definition: a small plate that moves separately within or beside a larger plate system
senses.definitionCN: 指在较大板块系统内部或旁边独立运动的小板块
senses.example: A small tectonic plate can rotate between two larger ones.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小构造板块可以在两个较大板块之间旋转。
senses.why: Finer surveying revealed pieces too small to appear on early world maps.
senses.whyCN: 更精细的测量揭示出早期世界地图上画不下的小块。

senses.title: A plate reconstructed for the past
senses.definition: a plate that existed in the geological past and is reconstructed from fragments
senses.definitionCN: 指地质历史上曾经存在、由岩石碎片复原出的板块
senses.example: The ancient tectonic plate is known only from scattered fragments.
senses.exampleCN: 这个古老构造板块只能从零散碎片中推知。
senses.why: Old plates leave seams and fossils rather than outlines, so they must be pieced together.
senses.whyCN: 古老板块留下的是缝合带与化石而非轮廓，所以只能拼合复原。

senses.title: A unit in a classroom model
senses.definition: one piece of a simplified model used to demonstrate plate behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指演示板块行为时所用简化模型中的一块
senses.example: In the classroom model, each tectonic plate is a curved cardboard shell.
senses.exampleCN: 在课堂模型里，每个构造板块都是一片弯曲的纸板壳。
senses.why: The real slab is hundreds of kilometres thick, so teaching models shrink it to something cuttable.
senses.whyCN: 真实板块厚达数百公里，教学模型便把它缩小到可以剪裁的程度。

intro.en: Tectonic comes from Greek tekton, a builder or carpenter, through tektonikos, of building, and Latin tectonicus. English used it for architecture before geologists borrowed it for the building of the Earth's crust. Plate took a separate route from Greek platys, broad and flat, through a reconstructed Vulgar Latin form and Old French.
intro.cn: 「构造」一词来自希腊语中表示「建造者、木匠」的词，经表示「建造的」的形容词与拉丁语形式进入英语；英语先用它谈建筑，后来地质学家借它指地壳的拼装。「板块」另走一条路，从希腊语表示「宽而平」的词，经一种重构的通俗拉丁语形式与古法语进入英语。

items.en: Tekton meant a builder or carpenter, a craftsman who fits pieces together.
items.cn: 这个词意为建造者、木匠，即把构件装配起来的工匠。

items.en: The adjective described what belongs to building or construction.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述与建造、装配有关的事物。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective for things relating to building.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词，指与建造有关的事物。

items.en: English first used it in the seventeenth century for architecture; the geological sense arose in the nineteenth century, when the precise date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪先把它用于建筑；地质义在十九世纪出现，确切年份不确定。

items.en: Platys meant broad and flat; a reconstructed Vulgar Latin adjective supplied the later European words for a flat sheet.
items.cn: 这个词意为宽而平；一个重构的通俗拉丁语形容词提供了后来欧洲各语言中表示「平板」的词。

items.era: OLD FRENCH PLATE AND ENGLISH PLATE
items.en: Old French plate named a flat metal sheet, and English adopted it in the fourteenth century for flat dishes and sheets.
items.cn: 古法语中这个词指扁平金属板，英语在十四世纪借入，指平盘与平板。

note.en: The first group shares the building root or the flat-sheet shape; the second group names other pieces and edges of the lithosphere.
note.cn: 第一组共享「建造」词根或「平板」形状；第二组是岩石圈其他块体与边缘的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for building or for crustal structure, used alone.
entries.definitionCN: 指「建造的」或「地壳构造的」形容词，可单独使用。

entries.definition: A flat sheet, dish or slab; the noun inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指平板、盘子或厚板，是短语中的名词。

entries.definition: A broad raised area of land with a flat top.
entries.definitionCN: 指顶部平坦的高地。

entries.definition: A flat decorative or memorial plate fixed to a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指固定在表面上的扁平装饰板或纪念牌。

entries.definition: A large flat dish used for serving food.
entries.definitionCN: 指盛食物用的大平盘。

entries.definition: The technical synonym that names the layer the plate belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 技术同义词，点明板块所属的圈层。

entries.definition: A piece of crust considered as a unit, without the mantle part.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为整体看待的一块地壳，不含地幔部分。

entries.definition: The boundary zone at the edge of a plate.
entries.definitionCN: 指板块边缘的边界带。

entries.definition: A thick flat piece of solid material, the plain image behind the term.
entries.definitionCN: 指厚而平的一块固体材料，是该术语背后的朴素意象。

entries.definition: A small plate recognised within a larger system.
entries.definitionCN: 指较大系统中被识别出的小板块。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the builder and the flat board: a carpenter fitting large slabs into a curved shell.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「建造者」与「平板」展开：木匠把大块厚板装进一个曲面外壳。

normal.en: Builder plus flat sheet: a constructed slab, which is exactly what a plate is.
normal.cn: 建造者加平板：拼装成的厚板，正是板块的样子。

normal.en: The Pacific plate is the biggest piece in the mosaic.
normal.cn: 太平洋板块是这幅拼图中最大的一块。

normal.en: Oceanic plates are thin and heavy; continental plates are thick and light.
normal.cn: 大洋板块薄而重，大陆板块厚而轻。

normal.en: Earthquakes and volcanoes line the edges, not the middles.
normal.cn: 地震与火山沿边缘排列，而不是在板块中部。

normal.en: A classroom model cuts the shell into pieces you can hold.
normal.cn: 课堂模型把外壳剪成可以用手拿的块。

abstract.en: A rigid thing can still move, as long as everything beneath it is softer.
abstract.cn: 坚硬之物仍能移动，只要它下面的一切更柔软。

abstract.en: Most of the action in a system happens at its seams.
abstract.cn: 一个系统里的大部分动静都发生在接缝处。

abstract.en: Naming the pieces is how a theory turns a picture into a science.
abstract.cn: 给各块命名，是理论把一幅图变成一门科学的方式。

examples.en: Each tectonic plate moves on the mantle at about the speed a fingernail grows.
examples.cn: 每个构造板块在地幔上移动，速度约与指甲生长相当。

examples.en: The map colours every tectonic plate and marks the boundaries between them.
examples.cn: 这幅地图给每个构造板块上色，并标出它们之间的边界。

examples.en: A tectonic plate boundary is where most of the world's earthquakes occur.
examples.cn: 构造板块边界是世界大多数地震发生的地方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「泰克托尼克·普雷特」——建筑师把扁平石板拼成球面，一块块都是构造板块：板块、岩石圈板块

root: 「构造」出自希腊语 tekton「建造者、木匠」，经 tektonikos「建造的」与拉丁语 tectonicus 进入英语，十七世纪先指建筑，十九世纪转指地壳构造；「板块」出自希腊语 platys「宽而平」，经重构的通俗拉丁语形式与古法语 plate 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one slab: the lithosphere piece, the named plate, its ocean or continent version, its edge, its drift, and its smaller and older relatives.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项围绕同一块厚板展开：岩石圈中的那一块、具名板块、它的洋壳或陆壳版本、它的边缘、它的漂移，以及更小与更古老的同类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curved mosaic of thick stone slabs, each pressed against its neighbours, floating on a softer layer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅由厚石板拼成的球面拼图，每块都顶住邻块，浮在更软的一层之上。

branches.en: THE SLAB ITSELF: the rigid lithosphere piece, and the cut-down model used to teach it.
branches.cn: 厚板本身：坚硬的岩石圈块体，以及为教学剪小的模型。

branches.en: THE SIZES: the dozen named giants, and the small plates found between them.
branches.cn: 尺度之分：十来块具名巨板，以及夹在它们之间的小板块。

branches.en: THE TWO CRUSTS: heavy oceanic plates and buoyant continental plates.
branches.cn: 两种地壳：沉重的大洋板块与较轻的大陆板块。

branches.en: THE ACTIVE RIM: the boundary zone where plates meet, and the drift that carries them there.
branches.cn: 活动的边缘：板块相接的边界带，以及把它们送到那里的漂移。

branches.en: THE VANISHED PIECE: a plate known only from the fragments it left behind.
branches.cn: 消失的一块：只能凭遗留碎片推知的古老板块。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek building word to a Greek flatness word; Latin carried both into European languages.
intro.cn: 这条短语把一个希腊语「建造」词与一个希腊语「扁平」词连起来，拉丁语把两者带进欧洲各语言。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the building adjective from Greek, and a reconstructed Vulgar Latin adjective stands behind the flat-sheet word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入表示「建造」的形容词；表示「平板」的词背后是一个重构的通俗拉丁语形容词。

items.example: It supplies the first element of tectonic.
items.exampleCN: 它是「构造」一词的第一个成分。

items.example: It turned the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Latin passed the adjective to English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词传给英语。

items.example: The geological sense is a nineteenth-century extension.
items.exampleCN: 地质义是十九世纪的延伸。

items.example: It forms the name of the discipline, tectonics.
items.exampleCN: 它构成学科名「构造学」。

items.example: It is the distant source of plate.
items.exampleCN: 它是「板块」一词的远源。

items.example: The form is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式是重构的，并非直接见于文献。

items.example: English took it for dishes and sheets of metal.
items.exampleCN: 英语借它指盘子与金属板。

items.example: The compound names the whole theory.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成词指整套理论。

items.example: The prefix means small and the noun means plate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀意为「小」，名词意为「板块」。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊「建造」词加形容词词尾构成，义为「构造的」
由形容词加学科词尾构成，义为「构造地质学」
由希腊「扁平」词经拉丁语与古法语构成，义为「板；板块」
由「板块」与「构造学」组合而成，义为「板块构造学说」
由「微小」前缀加「板块」构成，义为「微板块」
由「板块」加「边缘」构成，义为「板块边缘」
由「板块」加「边界」构成，义为「板块边界」
由「构造」词干加表示作用的名词词尾构成，义为「构造作用」

definition_zh: v. 流出；涌出；散发 adj. （植物、贝壳）平展的；散开的
definition_en: to pour out or flow forth; to give off light, warmth or feeling in abundance
core_image: 石缝里一股细水不断涌出，在苔石上摊成一片亮面；灯罩向四周泼出暖黄的光；标本纸上一簇小花松散平展，枝条向四面摊开
scene: 山道旁的石缝里有一股细水不停涌出，在苔石上摊成一片发亮的水面。 Clear water effuses from the crack and spreads over the mossy stone.
sceneCN: 这里 effuse 指「像液体那样流出、涌出」（第 1 个义项：流出；涌出）；句意是清水从石缝里涌出，摊过苔石。图中可辨识物件：石缝、细水流、苔石、发亮水面。

senses.title: To pour forth
senses.definition: to pour out or flow forth

senses.example: Clear water effuses from the crack and spreads over the mossy stone.

senses.title: To give off in abundance
senses.definition: to send out light, warmth or feeling freely and in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: （动词）大量地发出光、热或情感
senses.example: The old lamp effuses a warm yellow light across the whole desk.
senses.exampleCN: 那盏旧灯向整张桌子散发出暖黄色的光。
senses.why: A lamp shade throwing warm yellow light out to every edge of a desk.

senses.title: Spread out loosely

intro.en: Effuse is Latin effusus, poured out, from effundere, which joins ex- meaning out to fundere meaning to pour; the same fus- root gives fusion, diffuse and infuse.
intro.cn: effuse 就是拉丁语 effusus（被倒出的），来自 effundere，它把 ex-（向外）与 fundere（倾倒）结合；同一个 fus- 词根给出 fusion、diffuse 与 infuse。

items.en: Latin fundere means to pour, with the participle fusus.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fundere 意为倾倒，分词为 fusus。

items.en: Adding ex- gives effundere, to pour out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 effundere，意为倒出。

items.en: The participle effusus means poured out.
items.cn: 分词 effusus 意为被倒出的。

items.en: English took effuse as a verb for pouring forth.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪把 effuse 用作「涌出」的动词。

items.en: The noun effusion named both a pouring out and an outburst of feeling.
items.cn: 名词 effusion 既指流出，也指情感的迸发。

items.en: Botanists used effuse for a flower cluster spread loosely open.
items.cn: 植物学家用 effuse 指松散平展的花序。

note.en: Effuse, confuse, diffuse and infuse all carry fus-, the Latin root for poured; the prefix says out, together, apart or in.
note.cn: effuse、confuse、diffuse 与 infuse 都带着 fus-，那是拉丁语「倾倒」的词根；前缀说明是向外、一起、分开还是向内。

dict_mnemonic.text: effuse ＝ ef-（向外，ex- 在 f 前的变体）＋ fuse（倾倒，拉丁 fundere／fusus）＝「向外倒」。记住 fus- 这一家按前缀分方向：ef-（外）→ effuse 流出、effusion 流出／积液、effusive 感情往外倒＝热情洋溢的；dif-（分开）→ diffuse 扩散；in-（向内）→ infuse 注入、泡茶；con-（一起）→ confuse 倒在一起＝混淆；pro-（向前）→ profuse 大量倾泻＝丰富的。日常英语里 effuse 作动词较少见，更常见的是 effusive（热情洋溢的）与 effusion（流出；积液）。植物学、贝壳学里 effuse 作形容词，指「松散平展的」。

definition_zh: 固有的；与生俱来的；字里隐含的；无法分离的；法律上固有的；材料本身具有的；逻辑上内含的；生物固有的
definition_en: existing as a natural and permanent part of something, so that it cannot be separated from it
core_image: 老屋墙脚总是渗着湿气，刷多少层漆都盖不住，湿气像是从石头里长出来的
scene: 老屋的墙脚总是渗着湿气，刷多少层漆都盖不住，那湿气像是从石头里长出来的。 Old stone walls have an inherent dampness that no paint can hide.
sceneCN: 这里指事物本身固有、靠外力去不掉的（第 1 个义项：作为某物天然组成部分而存在）；句意为老石墙自带一种漆也盖不住的潮气。

pos.zh: 固有的；内在的；与生俱来的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示方式的副词后缀构成，义为「固有地；本质上」
由该形容词的词干加表示状态的名词后缀构成，义为「固有；内在性」
由同一词干加另一表示性质的名词后缀构成，义为「固有性」，多用于哲学与法律
由拉丁 inhaerere 直接进入英语，义为「固有于；存在于」，是该词族的动词
同词根加表示「朝向」的前缀构成，义为「附着的；拥护者」，与目标词共享「粘住」的词根

senses.title: Existing as a natural part
senses.titleCN: 作为天然组成部分而存在
senses.definition: belonging to something so completely that it cannot be taken away without changing the thing
senses.definitionCN: 完全属于某物，取走就会改变该物，因而无法去除
senses.example: Every alloy has inherent limits on how far it can bend.
senses.exampleCN: 每种合金在弯曲程度上都有固有的极限。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to stick fast inside, so the adjective pictures a quality lodged in the material itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「牢牢粘在里面」，因此这个形容词画出一种卡在材料内部的素质。

senses.title: Present from birth in a person
senses.definition: part of a person's nature from birth rather than acquired by training
senses.definitionCN: 自出生起就是某人天性的一部分，而非训练所得
senses.example: She has an inherent sense of rhythm that lessons only refined.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一种与生俱来的节奏感，课程只是把它打磨得更细。
senses.why: What is stuck in a person from the start cannot be attributed to later learning.
senses.whyCN: 从一开始就「粘」在人身上的东西，不能归因于后来的学习。

senses.title: Implied in the meaning of words
senses.definition: contained in the meaning of a term even when it is not stated openly
senses.definitionCN: 即使没有明说，也包含在一个词项的意义之中
senses.example: The word 'alone' carries an inherent suggestion of sadness.
senses.exampleCN: 「独自」这个词本身就隐含一丝悲凉。
senses.why: A meaning can hold another meaning inside it, the same way a substance holds a quality.
senses.whyCN: 一个意义可以把另一个意义包在里面，正如一种物质含有某种性质。

senses.title: A risk that cannot be separated
senses.definition: a danger or weakness built into an activity so that avoiding it would mean abandoning the activity
senses.definitionCN: 活动本身带来的危险或缺陷，避开它就等于放弃这项活动
senses.example: Some risk is inherent in any surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 任何手术都存在某种固有风险。
senses.why: If the risk comes attached to the practice, no amount of care removes it entirely.
senses.whyCN: 若风险随这项实践一同附着而来，再小心也无法彻底去掉它。

senses.title: A right that belongs by office
senses.titleCN: 因职位本身而有的权利
senses.definition: a power or right held because of the nature of an office or a legal position
senses.definitionCN: 因职位或法律地位的性质而拥有的权力或权利
senses.example: The court has an inherent power to control its own process.
senses.exampleCN: 法院拥有管理自身程序的固有权力。
senses.why: Legal English treats certain powers as attached to the office rather than granted by a separate document.
senses.whyCN: 法律英语把某些权力看作附着于职位本身，而不是由另一份文件授予。

senses.title: A property of the material itself
senses.definition: a physical property that comes from the substance, not from how it is shaped or used
senses.definitionCN: 由物质本身而来的物理性质，而非由形状或用途造成
senses.example: Rust resistance is inherent in stainless steel.
senses.exampleCN: 抗锈性是不锈钢本身固有的。
senses.why: Testing separates what the substance brings from what the process adds, and the former is inherent.
senses.whyCN: 检测要把物质自带的与工艺添加的区分开，前者就是固有的。

senses.title: A contradiction contained within
senses.definition: a conflict that follows from the very definition of a system, so it cannot be removed by adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 由体系定义本身推出的冲突，无法靠调整消除
senses.example: Critics point to an inherent contradiction in the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者指出这项政策存在内在矛盾。
senses.why: Logic can hold one statement inside another, and a conflict so held is inherent rather than accidental.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑可以把一个陈述包在另一个里，这样被包住的冲突就是内在的，而非偶然的。

senses.title: Defence present from the start
senses.definition: said of biological protection that an organism is born with, as opposed to acquired immunity
senses.definitionCN: 用于生物体天生具备的保护，与后天获得的免疫相对
senses.example: Inherent immunity blocks many bacteria before antibodies form.
senses.exampleCN: 在抗体形成之前，固有免疫就已挡住许多细菌。
senses.why: The body's first line is already in place, so medicine calls it inherent rather than learned.
senses.whyCN: 身体的第一道防线早已就位，因此医学称它为固有的，而不是后天学来的。

intro.en: Inherent comes from Latin inhaerere 'to stick in', built on in- 'in' and haerere 'to stick, to cling'. Its participle inhaerens gave the adjective, which English took in the seventeenth century. The same root yields adhere and hesitate.
intro.cn: inherent 来自拉丁 inhaerere「粘在里面」，由 in-「在内」与 haerere「粘住」构成。其分词 inhaerens 给出形容词，英语十七世纪引入。同一词根还产生 adhere 与 hesitate。

items.en: Haerere meant to stick, to cling or to be stuck fast, and it could describe both glue and a stalled mind.
items.cn: haerere 意为粘住、附着或卡住不动，既能形容胶，也能形容卡住的思路。

items.en: With in- 'in', inhaerere meant to stick inside something, and it described qualities that cling to a subject.
items.cn: 加 in-「在内」，inhaerere 意为粘在内部，用来描述附着于主体的性质。

items.en: The participle inhaerens named what inheres, and philosophy used it for properties that belong to a substance.
items.cn: 分词 inhaerens 命名「内居的东西」，哲学用它指属于实体的属性。

items.en: English adopted the adjective in theology and natural philosophy before it became an everyday word.
items.cn: 英语在神学与自然哲学中先采用这个形容词，之后才成为日常用词。

items.en: Law uses inherent for powers and rights attached to an office, not created by a separate grant.
items.cn: 法律用这个词指附着于职位的权力与权利，而非由另一次授予创造。

items.en: Inherent stresses the attachment to a subject; intrinsic stresses what lies within a thing's own nature, apart from anything external.
items.cn: inherent 强调「附着于主体」；intrinsic 强调「属于事物自身本质内部、与外来因素无关」。

note.en: The first group shares the clinging stem; the second group holds the words most often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组共享「粘住」词干；第二组列出最容易被它与混淆的几个词。

entries.definition: To exist as a permanent quality in something; the verb behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 作为永久性质存在于某物之中；是形容词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The state of existing inside something as a quality; a formal philosophical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 作为性质存在于某物内部的状态；正式的哲学名词。

entries.definition: By its own nature; it marks a judgement about what cannot be changed.
entries.definitionCN: 就其本性而言；标出「无法改变」这一判断。

entries.definition: Sticking to a surface, or a person who supports a cause; it adds the idea of attaching from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 附着在表面上，或指拥护某个主张的人；多了「从外部贴上」之意。

entries.definition: Belonging to a thing's own inner nature, measured without reference to anything outside; it stresses the inside rather than the attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物自身的内在本质，不参照外部来量度；强调「内部」而非「附着」。

entries.definition: Present from birth, used mainly of living things and abilities; it marks origin in time rather than inseparability.
entries.definitionCN: 出生时即有，主要用于生物与能力；标出时间上的来源，而非不可分离。

entries.definition: Belonging to the essence, so that without it the thing would not be what it is; stronger than mere attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 属于本质，缺了它事物就不成其为该物；比单纯「附着」更强。

entries.definition: Included as part of a product's design; the everyday compound for qualities installed rather than grown.
entries.definitionCN: 作为产品设计的一部分内置；是日常复合词，指装进去而非长出来的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'in' and the root means 'stick': inherent is stuck inside and will not come out.
normal.cn: 前缀是「在内」，词根是「粘」：固有的就是粘在里面取不出来。

normal.en: The family runs inhere, inherence, inherently and adherent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括固有、固有性、固有地、附着的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark risk and defect: inherent risk, inherent weakness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出风险与缺陷：固有风险、内在缺陷。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark law and logic: inherent right, inherent contradiction.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律与逻辑：固有权利、内在矛盾。

normal.en: Its nearest rival is intrinsic: inherent clings to a subject, intrinsic lies in its own nature.
normal.cn: 最接近的对手是 intrinsic：前者附着于主体，后者属于自身本质。

abstract.en: Picture moss growing inside a crack that no knife can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象青苔长在刀也够不到的裂缝里。

abstract.en: Picture a bell whose hum is part of its metal, not the air.
abstract.cn: 想象钟的余音来自金属本身，而不是空气。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that exists in the game itself, not on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则存在于游戏本身，而不是贴在墙上。

examples.en: There is an inherent danger in climbing without a rope.
examples.cn: 徒手攀爬存在固有危险。

examples.en: The design has an inherent flaw that no software patch can fix.
examples.cn: 这个设计存在任何补丁都修不好的内在缺陷。

examples.en: Patience is inherent in good teaching, not added later.
examples.cn: 耐心是好教学本身固有的，而不是后来添上的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「印海里」——像印在海里一样去不掉，就是固有

root: 拉丁 haerere「粘住」→ inhaerere「粘在里面」→ 分词 inhaerens → 英语 inherent；同根词 adhere、hesitate、coherent。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a quality stuck inside its owner: in matter, in a person, in a meaning, in a practice, in an office, in logic or in a body's defences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「粘在所有者内部」的性质：在材料里、在人身上、在词义里、在实践里、在职位里、在逻辑里，或在身体的防御里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quality lodged inside a substance, impossible to peel off without destroying it.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡在物质内部的一种性质，剥下来就会毁掉该物。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL SIDE: what belongs to a substance or alloy rather than to its treatment.
branches.cn: 材料一面：属于物质或合金本身，而非加工带来的。

branches.en: THE PERSONAL SIDE: a trait present from birth.
branches.cn: 个人一面：出生时即有的特质。

branches.en: THE LINGUISTIC SIDE: a suggestion carried inside a word's meaning.
branches.cn: 语言一面：藏在词义里的暗示。

branches.en: THE BUILT-IN BURDEN: a risk tied to the practice, and a contradiction following from the definition.
branches.cn: 自带负担：与实践绑在一起的风险，以及由定义推出的矛盾。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTIONAL SIDE: powers held by an office, and defences present from the start.
branches.cn: 建制一面：职位自带的权利，以及从一开始就有的防御。

intro.en: Inherent is Latin in- 'in' plus haerere 'to stick', with the present participle ending -ens and the English adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: inherent 由拉丁 in-「在内」与 haerere「粘住」构成，带现在分词词尾 -ens 与英语形容词词尾 -ent。

latinIntro.en: Haerere 'to stick' gives inhaerere 'to stick in'; its participle inhaerens gives the adjective, and the same root gives adhere and hesitate.
latinIntro.cn: haerere「粘住」给出 inhaerere「粘在里面」；其分词 inhaerens 给出形容词，同一词根还给出 adhere 与 hesitate。

items.example: The prefix locates the sticking inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「粘」定位在内部。

items.example: The verb supplies the clinging image.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「粘附」的画面。

items.example: The compound verb is the family source.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是词族来源。

items.example: Philosophy used the participle for properties.
items.exampleCN: 哲学用这个分词指属性。

items.example: The ending makes the participle an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把分词变成形容词。

items.example: The ending gives inherence, the state of sticking in.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾给出「固有性」这一状态。

items.example: English added legal and scientific uses.
items.exampleCN: 英语加上了法律与科学用法。

items.example: The verb states the relation plainly.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词平实地陈述这种关系。

items.example: The adverb marks judgement by nature.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词标出「就本性而言」的判断。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of clinging.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀改变了「粘」的方向。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「固有地」
由该形容词词干加状态名词后缀构成，义为「固有性」
由同一词干加性质名词后缀构成，义为「固有性」
由拉丁 inhaerere 进入英语，义为「固有于」
同词根加「朝向」前缀构成，义为「附着的；拥护者」
